title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, Ya Xu, Cambridge University Press, 2020, book (ISBN 9781108724265)
note: The standard practitioner text from Microsoft, Google and LinkedIn experimentation leads. Part I motivating examples and Twyman's law; Part II metrics and the OEC; chapters on SRM and trustworthiness checks, A/A tests, variance reduction (CUPED), triggering, leakage and interference, long-term and novelty effects, ethics (Ch. 9). Short chapters, about 290 pages.
course_use: Core textbook for the whole unit; assign Ch. 1-3, 17-21 (statistics, A/A tests, pitfalls) as readings. Paperback approx. EUR 35; e-book via Cambridge Core, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Field Experiments: Design, Analysis, and Interpretation
author_source: Alan S. Gerber, Donald P. Green, W. W. Norton, 2012, book
note: Rigorous yet readable introduction to randomized field experiments: potential outcomes, sampling distributions, blocking and clustering, covariate adjustment, one-sided and two-sided noncompliance (relevant to ad exposure and ghost ads), attrition, interference/spillovers, heterogeneous effects, meta-analysis. Exercises with data online.
course_use: Methods backbone for the design and analysis sessions; Ch. 2-4 and 5-6 (noncompliance) as background readings. Paid approx. EUR 60-90, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Experimentation Works: The Surprising Power of Business Experiments
author_source: Stefan H. Thomke, Harvard Business Review Press, 2020, book (ISBN 9781633697102)
note: Managerial perspective on building an experimentation organization: Booking.com, Microsoft Bing, Amazon, IBM, Kohl's store-hours test; experimentation culture, leadership role, seven myths. Accessible for business students without statistics.
course_use: Background and discussion reading for the opening session (why experiment, culture); pairs with the HBR culture article. Paid approx. EUR 25.

title: Statistical Methods in Online A/B Testing: Statistics for Data-Driven Business Decisions and Risk Management in E-commerce
author_source: Georgi Z. Georgiev, independently published, 2019, book (ISBN 9781694079725), 302 pages
note: Builds the statistics of A/B tests from the ground up with website-testing examples: p-values, confidence intervals, one-sided tests, power and sample size, sequential testing (AGILE), multiple testing, risk-reward framing of test decisions. Author runs Analytics-Toolkit.com.
course_use: Reference for students writing power and sequential-testing labs in Python; selected chapters as reading. Paid approx. EUR 40.

title: Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences: An Introduction
author_source: Guido W. Imbens, Donald B. Rubin, Cambridge University Press, 2015, book
note: Authoritative potential-outcomes treatment of randomized experiments: Fisher exact p-values, Neyman repeated sampling, regression adjustment, stratified and paired designs, noncompliance. Part II (Ch. 4-11) is the classical randomized-experiment material.
course_use: Advanced background for the instructor and strong students (randomization inference lab). Paid, Cambridge Core e-book, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The Power of Experiments: Decision Making in a Data-Driven World
author_source: Michael Luca, Max H. Bazerman, MIT Press, 2020, book
note: Business-school narrative on experiments at tech firms and in policy: Uber, Airbnb discrimination experiments, eBay paid search, Facebook emotional contagion debate, behavioural insights units. Short (about 230 pages), good for ethics and external-validity discussions.
course_use: Discussion reading for the ethics session; non-technical. Paid approx. EUR 25.

title: Practical Statistics for Data Scientists (2nd ed.) / Praktische Statistik für Data Scientists
author_source: Peter Bruce, Andrew Bruce, Peter Gedeck, O'Reilly, 2020 (German edition O'Reilly/dpunkt 2021), book
note: Ch. 3 Statistical Experiments and Significance Testing covers A/B testing, permutation tests, t-tests, multiple testing, power and sample size and multi-armed bandits, with Python and R code. German edition available for German-language courses.
course_use: Python lab companion for business students; Ch. 3 as hands-on reading. Paid approx. EUR 45; O'Reilly Learning, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Causal Inference in Python: Applying Causal Inference in the Tech Industry
author_source: Matheus Facure, O'Reilly, 2023, book; free companion online book Causal Inference for the Brave and True
note: Python-first causal inference for industry: randomized experiments, regression and CUPED-style variance reduction, heterogeneous effects and uplift (CATE, meta-learners), plus geo and switchback-type designs in the book. All notebooks open source.
course_use: Lab material for Python sessions on variance reduction and uplift; free online version, print approx. EUR 55.

title: The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality
author_source: Nick Huntington-Klein, Chapman and Hall/CRC, 2021 (2nd ed. 2025), book, free online
note: Very readable causal inference text; Ch. 10 treatment effects, chapter on experiments, with Python, R and Stata code. Useful bridge from A/B tests to quasi-experiments (DiD, synthetic control) for geo tests.
course_use: Free background reading for students without econometrics; experiments chapter as reading. Free online, print approx. EUR 50.

title: Causal Inference: The Mixtape
author_source: Scott Cunningham, Yale University Press, 2021, book, free online
note: Ch. 4 Potential Outcomes Causal Model covers randomization, SUTVA and Fisher exact tests; later chapters on DiD and synthetic control are relevant for matched-market and geo experiments. Python and R code.
course_use: Free supplementary reading; randomization-inference lab. Free online, print approx. EUR 35.

title: Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI
author_source: Victor Chernozhukov, Christian Hansen, Nathan Kallus, Martin Spindler, Vasilis Syrgkanis, online book, 2024
note: Free graduate-level book with Python notebooks: randomized experiments with covariate adjustment, double machine learning, heterogeneous treatment effects and policy learning. Spindler (Hamburg) makes it relevant to the German-speaking community.
course_use: Advanced reading for the uplift and HTE session; notebooks reusable in labs. Free.

title: Bandit Algorithms
author_source: Tor Lattimore, Csaba Szepesvari, Cambridge University Press, 2020, book, free PDF from authors
note: Comprehensive reference on multi-armed bandits (UCB, Thompson sampling, contextual bandits). Mathematically demanding; Ch. 1-4 and 36 (Thompson sampling) are the parts usable for marketing students.
course_use: Instructor background for adaptive experiments session. Free PDF; print approx. EUR 60.

title: Bandit Algorithms for Website Optimization
author_source: John Myles White, O'Reilly, 2012, book (about 90 pages)
note: Short, code-driven introduction to epsilon-greedy, softmax and UCB for website testing, with simulation framework. Code originally Python 2 and Julia, easy to port.
course_use: Lab template: students simulate bandits vs. fixed A/B split in Python. Paid approx. EUR 20; O'Reilly Learning, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A/B Testing: The Most Powerful Way to Turn Clicks Into Customers
author_source: Dan Siroker, Pete Koomen, Wiley, 2013, book
note: Optimizely founders' practitioner book; Obama 2008 campaign landing-page tests, what to test, building a testing culture. Dated on statistics (fixed-horizon peeking issues later fixed by Optimizely's Stats Engine).
course_use: Practitioner warm-up reading and source of classroom examples; contrast with Johari et al. on peeking. Paid approx. EUR 25.

title: Python for Marketing Research and Analytics
author_source: Jason S. Schwarz, Chris Chapman, Elea McDonnell Feit, Springer, 2020, book
note: Marketing analytics in Python with chapters on comparing groups, statistical tests, regression and Bayesian methods; Feit is co-author of the Test and Roll paper. Simulated marketing datasets suited to business students.
course_use: Python lab foundation for students before the A/B test analysis sessions. SpringerLink e-book, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Running Randomized Evaluations: A Practical Guide
author_source: Rachel Glennerster, Kudzai Takavarasha, Princeton University Press, 2013, book
note: J-PAL guide on the practical side of field experiments: choosing randomization unit, power (Ch. 6), threats (spillovers, attrition, noncompliance), ethics. Development context but transferable to store and geo tests.
course_use: Background for designing retail or store-level field experiments; power chapter as reading. Paid approx. EUR 40.

title: The Voltage Effect: How to Make Good Ideas Great and Great Ideas Scale
author_source: John A. List, Currency (Penguin Random House), 2022, book
note: Field-experiment pioneer (Uber, Lyft chief economist) on why effects shrink at scale: false positives, unrepresentative samples, spillovers. Directly addresses external validity of marketing experiments.
course_use: Discussion reading on external validity and scaling; popular-science level. Paid approx. EUR 20.

title: Empirical Generalizations about Marketing Impact (2nd ed.)
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens (ed.), Marketing Science Institute, 2015, book/report
note: Compilation of benchmark elasticities and effect sizes for advertising, price and promotion. Useful as realistic priors for minimum detectable effect and power calculations in marketing experiments.
course_use: Background for setting realistic MDEs in power labs. MSI members or purchase; check availability.

title: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook
author_source: Brett R. Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava, Dan Chapsky, Marketing Science 38(2), 193-225, 2019, article
note: 15 Facebook conversion-lift RCTs (1.6 bn impressions) compared with observational methods (matching, regression, inverse probability weighting): observational methods mostly overestimate lift. Key paper for why incrementality needs experiments.
course_use: Core reading for the ad-effectiveness session; class discussion on RCT vs. observational attribution. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen; working paper free on SSRN.

title: Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement
author_source: Brett R. Gordon, Robert Moakler, Florian Zettelmeyer, Marketing Science 42(4), 768-793, 2023, article
note: Follow-up with about 600 Facebook experiments: double/debiased ML and rich features still fail to recover experimental lift reliably. Updates the 2019 finding with modern ML methods.
course_use: Advanced reading paired with Gordon et al. 2019; supports debate on whether ML can replace experiments. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Test and Roll: Profit-Maximizing A/B Tests
author_source: Elea McDonnell Feit and Ron Berman, Marketing Science 38(6), 1038-1058, 2019
note: Reframes A/B tests as a profit decision: optimal test size is much smaller than hypothesis-testing sample sizes when the population is small or responses noisy. Three marketing applications (website design, display advertising, catalogue mailing) with priors from past tests; free preprint on arXiv (1811.00457) and online calculator.
course_use: Advanced session on sample size; students compare power-based vs. test-and-roll sizes in Python. Free preprint; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Ghost Ads: Improving the Economics of Measuring Online Ad Effectiveness
author_source: Garrett A. Johnson, Randall A. Lewis, Elmar I. Nubbemeyer, Journal of Marketing Research 54(6), 867-884, 2017, article
note: Introduces ghost ads and predicted ghost ads: logging would-be exposures in the control group to measure ad lift without paying for PSA ads; application with a retailer on Google Display Network. Paul E. Green and Weitz-Winer-O'Dell awards.
course_use: Core reading for incrementality measurement design (intent-to-treat vs. treatment-on-treated). WU-Lizenz prüfen; SSRN version free.

title: The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising
author_source: Randall A. Lewis, Justin M. Rao, Quarterly Journal of Economics 130(4), 1941-1973, 2015, article
note: 25 large field experiments with US retailers and brokerages: median ROI confidence interval wider than 100 percentage points; explains why ad effects are hard to detect given noisy sales. Excellent motivation for power analysis.
course_use: Reading for the power and sample size session; classroom calculation of required sample size for ad lift. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Online Ads and Offline Sales: Measuring the Effect of Retail Advertising via a Controlled Experiment on Yahoo!
author_source: Randall A. Lewis, David H. Reiley, Quantitative Marketing and Economics 12(3), 235-266, 2014, article
note: Randomized experiment with 1.6 million customers of a major retailer linking online display ads to in-store sales; ads increased purchases by about 5 percent, mostly offline. Classic omnichannel retail ad experiment.
course_use: Reading for retail ad effectiveness; illustrates matching online exposure to offline sales. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: When Less Is More: Data and Power in Advertising Experiments
author_source: Garrett A. Johnson, Randall A. Lewis, David H. Reiley, Marketing Science 36(1), 2017, article
note: Shows how to gain statistical power in ad experiments by filtering out noise (e.g. restricting to exposed users and relevant outcome windows); Yahoo retail experiment.
course_use: Reading for variance reduction in ad experiments; pairs with CUPED. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Consumer Heterogeneity and Paid Search Effectiveness: A Large-Scale Field Experiment
author_source: Thomas Blake, Chris Nosko and Steven Tadelis, 'Consumer Heterogeneity and Paid Search Effectiveness: A Large-Scale Field Experiment', Econometrica 83(1), 155-174, 2015
note: eBay stopped brand-keyword ads and ran geo-randomised non-brand experiments: brand ads have no measurable short-term benefit; non-brand ads help only new/infrequent users, average returns negative. Observational estimates hugely overstated ROI. Accessible summaries: VoxEU column and Chicago Booth Review; free working paper at faculty.haas.berkeley.edu/stadelis/BNT_ECMA_rev.pdf.
course_use: Core example for incrementality vs. attribution; discussion: why did eBay's agency report positive ROI? Paywalled journal, NBER w20171 free; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments by Utilizing Pre-Experiment Data (CUPED)
author_source: Alex Deng, Ya Xu, Ron Kohavi, Toby Walker, WSDM 2013 (Proceedings of the 6th ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining), 123-132, conference paper
note: Introduces CUPED, a control-variate estimator using pre-period metrics; about 50 percent variance reduction on Bing. Now standard in all experimentation platforms.
course_use: Reading plus Python lab: implement CUPED on simulated or e-commerce data and compare confidence interval widths. Free PDF on exp-platform.com.

title: Controlled Experiments on the Web: Survey and Practical Guide
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Roger Longbotham, Dan Sommerfield, Randal M. Henne, Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 18(1), 140-181, 2009, article
note: Foundational survey of web A/B testing: OEC, power and sample size, A/A tests, ramp-up, randomization and hashing, limitations; HiPPO concept. Free PDF from Stanford.
course_use: Introductory reading for the first session. Open access via author PDF.

title: Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: Five Puzzling Outcomes Explained
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Alex Deng, Brian Frasca, Roger Longbotham, Toby Walker, Ya Xu, KDD 2012, conference paper
note: Five real Bing puzzles (e.g. a bug that raised revenue, carryover effects, misleading metrics) and their root causes. Great case material on Twyman's law and metric choice.
course_use: Discussion session: students diagnose each puzzle before reading the explanation. Free author PDF.

title: Seven Rules of Thumb for Web Site Experimenters
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Alex Deng, Roger Longbotham, Ya Xu, KDD 2014, conference paper
note: Empirical rules from thousands of experiments: small changes can have big impact, changes rarely have big positive impact, your mileage will vary, speed matters, reducing abandonment is hard, avoid complex designs, ensure enough users.
course_use: Short reading for intuition-building; slides and video on exp-platform.com/rules-of-thumb. Free author PDF.

title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments: A Taxonomy and Rules of Thumb for Practitioners
author_source: Aleksander Fabijan, Jayant Gupchup, Somit Gupta, Jeff Omhover, Wen Qin, Lukas Vermeer, Pavel Dmitriev, KDD 2019, conference paper
note: Taxonomy of SRM causes (assignment, execution, log processing, analysis, interference) from Booking.com, Microsoft, Outreach and Online Dialogue; chi-square SRM check.
course_use: Lab: students run an SRM chi-square test before analysing a dataset. Free PDF on exp-platform.com.

title: Top Challenges from the First Practical Online Controlled Experiments Summit
author_source: Somit Gupta, Ronny Kohavi, Diane Tang, Ya Xu et al., SIGKDD Explorations 21(1), 20-35, 2019, article
note: 34 experts from 13 firms (Amazon, Booking, Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Netflix, Uber ...) list open problems: OEC and long-term effects, heterogeneous effects, interference in marketplaces, culture. Good map of the field.
course_use: Overview reading or group presentations (one challenge per team). Free.

title: Statistical Challenges in Online Controlled Experiments: A Review of A/B Testing Methodology
author_source: Nicholas Larsen, Jonathan Stallrich, Srijan Sengupta, Alex Deng, Ron Kohavi, Nathaniel T. Stevens, The American Statistician 78(2), 135-149, 2024, article
note: Up-to-date statistical review: variance reduction, heterogeneous effects, sequential testing and peeking, interference, long-term effects, small-sample and heavy-tail issues. Open access on arXiv (2212.11366).
course_use: Instructor reference and advanced student reading; good structure for a methods lecture. Open access.

title: Always Valid Inference: Continuous Monitoring of A/B Tests
author_source: Ramesh Johari, Pete Koomen, Leonid Pekelis, David Walsh, Operations Research 70(3), 1806-1821, 2022, article
note: Shows how peeking inflates false positives and derives always-valid p-values (mSPRT) implemented in Optimizely's Stats Engine.
course_use: Reading for the peeking and sequential testing session; Python simulation of peeking inflation. WU-Lizenz prüfen; arXiv preprint free.

title: False Discovery in A/B Testing
author_source: Ron Berman, Christophe Van den Bulte, Management Science 68(9), 6762-6782, 2022, article
note: 4,964 effects from 2,766 Optimizely experiments: about 70 percent true nulls, false discovery rate 18-25 percent at 5 percent significance. Implications for multiple testing and two-stage designs.
course_use: Reading for multiple testing and false discoveries; discussion of what significant results mean in practice. Author PDF free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A/B Testing with Fat Tails
author_source: Eduardo M. Azevedo, Alex Deng, Jose Luis Montiel Olea, Justin Rao, E. Glen Weyl, Journal of Political Economy 128(12), 4614-4672, 2020, article
note: Uses Bing experiment data to show innovation effects are fat-tailed; optimal strategy then is many small, lean experiments rather than few large ones. Links experimentation to innovation strategy.
course_use: Advanced reading on experimentation strategy and portfolio of tests. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Experimentation and Start-up Performance: Evidence from A/B Testing
author_source: Rembrand Koning, Sharique Hasan, Aaron Chatterji, Management Science 68(9), 2022, article
note: Panel of tech start-ups: adopting A/B testing tools raises performance by 30-100 percent after a year, via more product launches and faster failure. Evidence that experimentation pays off at firm level.
course_use: Reading for the business case and culture session. NBER WP w26278 free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The Surprising Power of Online Experiments
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Stefan Thomke, Harvard Business Review 95(5), September-October 2017, 74-82, article
note: Managerial introduction: Bing headline test worth over 100 million USD, Amazon credit-card offer move, only 10-20 percent of tests positive at Google and Bing, OEC and pitfalls.
course_use: First-session reading for business students. HBR, WU-Lizenz prüfen (Business Source Premier); reprint PDF circulates.

title: Building a Culture of Experimentation
author_source: Stefan Thomke, Harvard Business Review 98(2), March-April 2020, article
note: Booking.com runs about 25,000 tests per year; describes democratized experimentation, the 2017 radical homepage redesign test, and leadership behaviours that enable experimentation.
course_use: Discussion reading on organization and culture. HBR, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Smart Business Experiments
author_source: Eric T. Anderson, Duncan Simester, Harvard Business Review 89(3), 98-105, March 2011, article
note: Seven rules for marketing field experiments (e.g. focus on individual customers, use control groups, exploit natural experiments) with catalog and retail pricing examples.
course_use: Short managerial reading for designing a student field-experiment proposal. HBR, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Field Experimentation in Marketing Research
author_source: Ayelet Gneezy, Journal of Marketing Research 54(1), 140-143, 2017, article (special section on field experiments)
note: Short argument for more field experiments in marketing, their defining features and practical considerations. Introduces the JMR 2017 special section on field experiments (a useful reading pool).
course_use: Short opening reading; point students to the special section for project ideas. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Field Experiments in Marketing
author_source: Duncan Simester, in: Handbook of Economic Field Experiments Vol. 1 (eds. Banerjee and Duflo), Elsevier, Ch. 11, 465-497, 2017, book chapter
note: Survey of marketing field experiments on pricing, advertising, product and model validation, both online and in physical stores, by a leading retail experimenter.
course_use: Background reading to map the literature; good reading list source. ScienceDirect, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: The Econometrics of Randomized Experiments
author_source: Susan Athey, Guido W. Imbens, in: Handbook of Economic Field Experiments Vol. 1, Elsevier, Ch. 3, 2017, book chapter (arXiv 1607.00698)
note: Design-based analysis of randomized experiments: randomization inference, stratification, clustering, regression adjustment, heterogeneous effects and network experiments. Free preprint.
course_use: Instructor background for the analysis sessions. Free on arXiv.

title: Effects of $9 Price Endings on Retail Sales: Evidence from Field Experiments
author_source: Eric T. Anderson, Duncan I. Simester, Quantitative Marketing and Economics 1(1), 93-110, 2003, article
note: Three catalog field experiments manipulating price endings: $9 endings increased demand, more for new items. Classic retail pricing experiment with simple design.
course_use: Reading for pricing experiments; replicate the analysis logic in class. Author PDF free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Competitive Price Targeting with Smartphone Coupons
author_source: Jean-Pierre Dube, Zheng Fang, Nathan Fong, Xueming Luo, Marketing Science 36(6), 944-975, 2017, article
note: Large mobile field experiment with two rival movie theatres randomizing coupon prices by location and past behaviour; traces out best-response functions and shows competitive effects of targeting.
course_use: Reading for price and promotion experiments and personalization. NBER WP free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Personalization in Email Marketing: The Role of Noninformative Advertising Content
author_source: Navdeep S. Sahni, S. Christian Wheeler, Pradeep K. Chintagunta, Marketing Science 37(2), 236-258, 2018, article
note: Randomized email experiments with three firms and millions of recipients: adding the recipient's name to the subject line raises opens and sales leads and reduces unsubscribes.
course_use: Reading and template for an email A/B test lab. SSRN version free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Estimating Marketing Component Effects: Double Machine Learning from Targeted Digital Promotions
author_source: Paul B. Ellickson, Wreetabrata Kar, James C. Reeder III, Marketing Science 42(4), 704-728, 2023, article
note: Decomposes effects of targeted email promotions (content, framing, discount type) along the funnel with double ML; clearance-framed discounts outperform product-specific ones.
course_use: Advanced reading on analysing many promotion variants. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: When Does Retargeting Work? Information Specificity in Online Advertising
author_source: Anja Lambrecht, Catherine Tucker, Journal of Marketing Research 50(5), 561-576, 2013, article
note: Field experiment with a travel website: dynamic (product-specific) retargeting underperforms generic retargeting unless consumers' preferences are well defined. O'Dell Award.
course_use: Reading on ad personalization experiments and heterogeneous effects. Author version free at LBS; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Customer Acquisition via Display Advertising Using Multi-Armed Bandit Experiments
author_source: Eric M. Schwartz, Eric T. Bradlow, Peter S. Fader, Marketing Science 36(4), 500-522, 2017, article
note: Hierarchical Thompson sampling to allocate display impressions across ad creatives and sites in a live campaign; about 8 percent more customer acquisitions than balanced A/B testing.
course_use: Core reading for the bandit session; Python lab simulating Thompson sampling vs. A/B. Penn repository version free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling
author_source: Daniel J. Russo, Benjamin Van Roy, Abbas Kazerouni, Ian Osband, Zheng Wen, Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 11(1), 1-96, 2018, article/monograph
note: Accessible tutorial on Thompson sampling with Bernoulli bandit examples, product recommendation and assortment; Ch. 1-3 suitable for business students with probability basics.
course_use: Reading for adaptive experiments; Bernoulli bandit example as lab. Free on arXiv.

title: Website Morphing
author_source: John R. Hauser, Glen L. Urban, Guilherme Liberali, Michael Braun, Marketing Science 28(2), 202-223, 2009, article
note: Early marketing application of bandits (Gittins index) to adapt website look and feel to inferred cognitive styles; BT broadband field test.
course_use: Background on adaptive personalization in marketing. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Retention Futility: Targeting High-Risk Customers Might Be Ineffective
author_source: Eva Ascarza, Journal of Marketing Research 55(1), 80-98, 2018, article
note: Two field experiments plus ML: customers with highest churn risk are not the ones most responsive to retention offers; target on uplift (treatment effect), not risk. Paul E. Green Award.
course_use: Core reading for uplift modeling; motivates CATE-based targeting lab. SSRN version free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects using Random Forests
author_source: Stefan Wager, Susan Athey, Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(523), 1228-1242, 2018, article
note: Introduces causal forests with valid confidence intervals for heterogeneous treatment effects; basis of the grf and EconML implementations.
course_use: Methods reference for the HTE session; students apply causal forest (EconML) to experiment data. arXiv version free.

title: Heterogeneous Treatment Effects and Optimal Targeting Policy Evaluation
author_source: Guenter J. Hitsch, Sanjog Misra, Walter W. Zhang, Quantitative Marketing and Economics 22, 115-168, 2024, article
note: Framework for targeting from randomized experiments: CATE estimation with ML methods, off-policy evaluation of targeting policies, profit comparisons on a large catalog-retailer experiment.
course_use: Advanced reading linking A/B tests to targeting policies. SpringerLink, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Targeting Prospective Customers: Robustness of Machine-Learning Methods to Typical Data Challenges
author_source: Duncan Simester, Artem Timoshenko, Spyros I. Zoumpoulis, Management Science 66(6), 2495-2522, 2020, article
note: Two large field experiments at a retailer: train seven ML targeting methods on the first, validate the targeting policies in the second. Shows effects of covariate shift and concept shift.
course_use: Reading on experiment-based targeting and external validity across waves. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Efficiently Evaluating Targeting Policies: Improving on Champion vs. Challenger Experiments
author_source: Duncan Simester, Artem Timoshenko, Spyros I. Zoumpoulis, Management Science 66(8), 3412-3424, 2020, article
note: Shows that comparing targeting policies only on customers where they disagree gives large precision gains over standard champion-vs-challenger tests.
course_use: Short reading for a design-efficiency discussion. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Causal Inference and Uplift Modelling: A Review of the Literature
author_source: Pierre Gutierrez, Jean-Yves Gerardy, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 67 (PAPIs 2016), 1-13, 2017, conference paper
note: Compact review of uplift approaches (two-model, class transformation, uplift trees) and evaluation with Qini and uplift curves. Practitioner-friendly.
course_use: Reading before an uplift-modeling lab (e.g. with the Hillstrom email dataset). Free.

title: Design and Analysis of Switchback Experiments
author_source: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, Jinglong Zhao, Management Science 69(7), 3759-3777, 2023, article
note: Optimal design and randomization-based inference for switchback (time-alternating) experiments under carryover effects; motivated by marketplace and pricing tests.
course_use: Reading for experiments under interference (marketplaces, delivery, dynamic pricing). WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Experimental Design in Two-Sided Platforms: An Analysis of Bias
author_source: Ramesh Johari, Hannah Li, Inessa Liskovich, Gabriel Y. Weintraub, Management Science 68(10), 7069-7089, 2022, article
note: Shows how interference in two-sided marketplaces biases customer-side and listing-side randomization, and when each design is less biased.
course_use: Reading on interference and SUTVA violations in marketplaces. WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: From Infrastructure to Culture: A/B Testing Challenges in Large Scale Social Networks
author_source: Ya Xu, Nanyu Chen, Addrian Fernandez, Omar Sinno, Anmol Bhasin, KDD 2015, conference paper
note: LinkedIn's experimentation platform (XLNT): scaling, metrics, network effects and building experimentation culture.
course_use: Industry case reading on platforms and culture. Free author PDF.

title: Focusing on the Long-term: It's Good for Users and Business
author_source: Henning Hohnhold, Deirdre O'Brien, Diane Tang, KDD 2015, 1849-1858, conference paper
note: Google method for measuring long-term user learning (ads blindness) with long-running holdouts; led to 50 percent ad load reduction on mobile. Central for novelty and long-term effects and OEC choice.
course_use: Reading on short-term vs. long-term metrics. Free PDF.

title: Experimental Evidence of Massive-Scale Emotional Contagion through Social Networks
author_source: Adam Kramer, Jamie Guillory and Jeffrey Hancock, PNAS 111(24), 2014
note: News feeds of 689,003 users were manipulated to show fewer positive or fewer negative posts; users then posted correspondingly. Public outrage over consent and manipulation; PNAS issued an editorial expression of concern. Classic case for the ethics of online experiments vs. 'normal' product tests.
course_use: Ethics debate: where is the line between A/B testing and manipulation? Pair with OkCupid. Open access.

title: Objecting to Experiments that Compare Two Unobjectionable Policies or Treatments
author_source: Michelle N. Meyer, Patrick R. Heck, Geoffrey S. Holtzman et al., PNAS 116(22), 10723-10728, 2019, article
note: 16 studies (n=5,873): people approve of implementing A or B untested but object to an A/B test comparing them (A/B effect). Follow-up debate in PNAS (Mislavsky et al.; 2023 replication).
course_use: Ethics discussion counterpoint to the Facebook study; classroom replication survey possible. Open access.

title: Shining a Light on Dark Patterns
author_source: Jamie Luguri, Lior Jacob Strahilevitz, Journal of Legal Analysis 13(1), 43-109, 2021, article
note: Randomized online experiments: mild dark patterns doubled, aggressive ones nearly quadrupled acceptance of a dubious subscription; less educated users more susceptible. Shows A/B testing used to optimize manipulation.
course_use: Ethics and regulation session reading. Open access.

title: Dark Patterns at Scale: Findings from a Crawl of 11K Shopping Websites
author_source: Arunesh Mathur, Gunes Acar, Michael J. Friedman, Elena Lucherini, Jonathan Mayer, Marshini Chetty, Arvind Narayanan, Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 3 (CSCW), 2019, article
note: Automated crawl finding 1,818 dark-pattern instances on e-commerce sites (fake urgency, scarcity, sneaking) and third-party vendors that sell them, many tied to optimization and testing tools.
course_use: Ethics session reading for retail e-commerce; dataset is public. Free on arXiv.

title: Online Controlled Experiments and A/B Testing
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Roger Longbotham, in: Encyclopedia of Machine Learning and Data Mining, Springer, 2017, encyclopedia entry
note: Concise (about 10 pages) definition-level overview of A/B testing terminology, OEC, pitfalls and history. Good glossary-style reading.
course_use: Short pre-reading before the first session. SpringerLink, WU-Lizenz prüfen; author PDF free.

title: A/B Testing: A Systematic Literature Review
author_source: Federico Quin, Danny Weyns, Matthias Galster, Camila Costa Silva, Journal of Systems and Software, 2024 (arXiv 2308.04929), article
note: Systematic review of 141 primary studies on A/B testing: subjects tested, designs, metrics, statistical methods, open problems. Software-engineering perspective complements the marketing literature.
course_use: Reference map for student literature reviews or seminar papers. Free on arXiv.

title: Measuring Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments
author_source: Jon Vaver and Jim Koehler, Google Inc. technical report, 2011
note: Google's method for randomising ad spend across geographic regions and estimating return on ad spend with a regression model; basis of later GeoLift/Meta and Google matched-markets tools. Good for offline and TV-like campaigns where users cannot be randomised.
course_use: Background for geo test design; link to Zalando location-based tests. Free. URL constructed from memory, verify.

title: Periodic Measurement of Advertising Effectiveness Using Multiple-Test-Period Geo Experiments
author_source: Jon Vaver, Jim Koehler, Google Inc., 2012, technical report
note: Extends geo experiments to repeated on/off test periods for ongoing measurement of campaign ROAS; useful design alternative when few regions exist (e.g. Austria's nine Bundeslaender).
course_use: Follow-up reading for advanced geo-experiment design. Free.

title: Estimating Ad Effectiveness using Geo Experiments in a Time-Based Regression Framework
author_source: Jouni Kerman, Peng Wang, Jon Vaver, Google Inc., 2017, technical report
note: Time-based regression (TBR) for matched-market geo tests with a single treatment and control aggregate; basis for Google's matched-markets tools.
course_use: Background for a matched-market lab. Free.

title: Online Choice Architecture: How Digital Design Can Harm Competition and Consumers
author_source: Competition and Markets Authority (UK), Discussion Paper CMA155, April 2022, government report
note: Taxonomy of 21 harmful choice-architecture practices (drip pricing, scarcity claims, sludge); discusses how firms use A/B testing to optimize such designs and how regulators can run their own experiments.
course_use: Ethics and regulation session reading; contrast commercial vs. regulatory testing. Free.

title: Dark Commercial Patterns
author_source: OECD, OECD Digital Economy Papers No. 336, 2022, report
note: International overview of dark patterns, evidence on prevalence and effects (including experimental studies) and policy responses in OECD countries including the EU.
course_use: Background for ethics session, European perspective. Free.

title: Behavioural Study on Unfair Commercial Practices in the Digital Environment: Dark Patterns and Manipulative Personalisation
author_source: European Commission, DG JUST (study by LE Europe, VVA, ConPolicy, Ipsos), 2022, government report
note: EU-wide mystery shopping of websites plus online behavioural experiments with consumers testing the effect of dark patterns and personalisation; relevant for EU legal context of A/B testing (UCPD, DSA).
course_use: Ethics and EU regulation reading; experiment design examples from a regulator. Free; link is a Publications Office search, check final URL.

title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
author_source: US Federal Trade Commission, Staff Report, September 2022, government report
note: FTC staff report on dark patterns in e-commerce and subscriptions with enforcement cases; useful contrast to EU approach.
course_use: Optional background for ethics debate. Free.

title: Bayesian A/B Testing at VWO (SmartStats technical white paper)
author_source: Chris Stucchio, Visual Website Optimizer (VWO), 2015, white paper
note: Explains Bayesian A/B testing with Beta-binomial posteriors, probability to beat control and expected loss decision rule as implemented in a commercial tool.
course_use: Reading for the Bayesian A/B testing lab (students implement expected-loss rule in Python). Free.

title: Evolution of Experimentation: Lessons from 127,000 Experiments
author_source: Optimizely, 2023, industry report
note: Benchmark report from a major testing vendor: win rates, typical uplifts, test velocity and which test types (e.g. personalization, multi-variant) perform better. Vendor data, interpret critically.
course_use: Discussion material on realistic effect sizes and win rates; compare with Berman and Van den Bulte. Free with registration; check exact report URL.

title: What Works in E-commerce: A Meta-Analysis of 6,700 Online Experiments
author_source: Will Browne, Mike Swarbrick Jones, Qubit, 2017, industry white paper
note: Meta-analysis of e-commerce A/B tests by treatment category (scarcity, social proof, urgency, cosmetic changes): most cosmetic changes have near-zero effect, scarcity and social proof have small positive effects.
course_use: Discussion on realistic effect sizes for retail website tests and on behavioural levers. Free; link is a Scholar search, original Qubit URL may have moved.

title: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement (MSI Report 18-113)
author_source: Brett R. Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava, Dan Chapsky, Marketing Science Institute Working Paper Series Report 18-113, 2018, report
note: Free report version of the Facebook conversion-lift study; describes Facebook's lift-test infrastructure and the gap between observational and experimental estimates. Freely downloadable alternative to the paywalled journal article.
course_use: Free substitute reading for students without journal access. Free PDF.

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test
author_source: Evan Miller, evanmiller.org, 2010, essay/reference page
note: The classic short explanation of the peeking problem: checking a running test repeatedly and stopping at significance inflates the false positive rate from 5% to well above 20%. Includes the n = 16 sigma^2/delta^2 rule of thumb. Companion pages on the low base rate problem and sequential testing on the same site.
course_use: Pre-reading for the session on test duration and stopping rules; replicate the peeking simulation in Python as a lab. Free.

title: Evan Miller's A/B Testing Tools: Sample Size Calculator
author_source: Evan Miller, evanmiller.org, interactive web tool (also chi-squared, sequential sampling and t-test tools)
note: Interactive calculator: enter baseline conversion rate, minimum detectable effect, power and alpha; returns sample size per variant. Widely used as the cross-check in CRO teams.
course_use: In-class demo before students compute the same numbers with statsmodels NormalIndPower; good for an exercise comparing relative vs absolute MDE. Free.

title: Experiment Guide (companion site to Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments)
author_source: Ron Kohavi, Diane Tang, Ya Xu, experimentguide.com, companion website to the Cambridge University Press book (2020)
note: Additional material, errata and free download of Chapter 1 in several languages (EN, ZH, RU, KO, PL). Chapter 1 gives the core vocabulary (OEC, randomisation unit, guardrails) plus motivating examples such as the Bing ad headline test.
course_use: Assign free Chapter 1 PDF as the opening reading; site as reference for students. Free (book itself paid, WU-Lizenz prüfen).

title: Microsoft Research Experimentation Platform (ExP): Articles
author_source: Microsoft Research, Experimentation Platform group, article series 2019-2026
note: Practitioner articles from the team that runs tens of thousands of experiments a year: Deep Dive Into Variance Reduction (2022), A/B Interactions: A Call to Relax (2023), External Validity of Online Experiments (2024), Event-based A/B tests, EU data protection and experimentation (2025). Includes the three-part Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation series (pre-, during-, post-experiment).
course_use: Background reading for the advanced session (variance reduction, interactions, external validity); the EU data protection article fits a European IB audience. Free.

title: Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation: Pre-Experiment Stage
author_source: Microsoft Research ExP, 2020, article (part 1 of 3; during- and post-experiment parts linked)
note: Checklist-style patterns for hypothesis and metric formulation and engineering choices that bias results; parts 2 and 3 cover SRM checks, monitoring and post-experiment learning. Very usable as a design checklist.
course_use: Use as checklist template for student experiment proposals (group project). Free.

title: statsmodels.stats.power: NormalIndPower.solve_power and proportion_effectsize
author_source: statsmodels developers, statsmodels.org, Python library documentation
note: Reference for solving for sample size, power, MDE or alpha of a two-sample z-test; combined with proportion_effectsize (Cohen's h) this is the standard Python route for conversion-rate test planning. Also tt_ind_solve_power for continuous metrics such as revenue per visitor.
course_use: Core reference for the Python lab on sample size planning. Free.

title: Causal Inference for the Brave and True, Chapter 2: Randomised Experiments
author_source: Matheus Facure (Nubank), free online book with Python notebooks, GitHub pages, 2021-2022
note: Light-hearted but rigorous open book; early chapters explain why randomisation solves selection bias and how to compute standard errors and CIs for A/B tests in Python; later chapters cover regression adjustment, heterogeneous effects and uplift, linking A/B testing to causal inference.
course_use: Reading plus notebooks for students who know pandas; bridges A/B testing to the causal inference block. Free, open source.

title: GrowthBook Statistics documentation
author_source: GrowthBook (open-source experimentation platform), docs.growthbook.io, documentation
note: Clear documentation of a Bayesian (default) and frequentist engine, sequential testing, CUPED, SRM detection, multiple-comparison corrections and custom priors; the Statistical Details page shows the formulas. Good for showing how a real tool computes Chance to Win vs confidence intervals.
course_use: Reference when comparing Bayesian vs frequentist output; GrowthBook is open source so students can self-host for a project. Free.

title: Optimizely Support: Statistical analysis methods overview (Stats Engine) and glossary
author_source: Optimizely, support.optimizely.com, knowledge base
note: Explains the three analysis modes Optimizely offers (fixed-horizon frequentist, Bayesian, sequential Stats Engine with false discovery rate control); glossary defines guardrail metrics, CUPED and other terms in marketer language.
course_use: Show students how a market-leading commercial tool frames statistics for marketers; compare with GrowthBook docs. Free.

title: Statsig Docs: Power Analysis
author_source: Statsig, docs.statsig.com, product documentation
note: Documents how a power calculator uses a metric's historical mean, variance and traffic to trade off MDE, duration and allocation, with week-by-week projections. Sister page on SRM checks (docs.statsig.com/stats-engine/methodologies/srm-checks).
course_use: Reference for the planning step of a student experiment design; compare with own statsmodels calculation. Free.

title: Eppo Docs: CUPED++
author_source: Eppo (Datadog), docs.geteppo.com, product documentation
note: Documentation of regression-based variance reduction using pre-experiment data and assignment properties; explains when CUPED helps and how CUPED++ extends it. Companion guide: running well-powered experiments with smaller samples.
course_use: Reference for the variance-reduction session alongside the Microsoft ExP deep dive. Free.

title: Google Ads Help: Set up a custom experiment / Experiments page
author_source: Google, Google Ads Help Center, documentation
note: How marketers run split tests on campaigns: traffic split (recommended 50/50), cookie-based vs search-based split, fixed split after setup, scaled reporting for uneven splits. Shows A/B testing inside an ad platform rather than on a website. Related FAQ: support.google.com/google-ads/answer/13826584.
course_use: Marketing application session: discuss what randomisation unit Google uses and threats to validity in platform experiments. Free (Google Ads account needed to try).

title: Google Ads API: Experiments overview
author_source: Google, developers.google.com, API documentation
note: Developer view of campaign experiments including campaign mix experiments; useful to show that ad-platform tests are programmable and how arms and splits are defined.
course_use: Optional reference for data-science oriented students. Free.

title: VWO SmartStats: Bayesian A/B Testing at VWO (technical whitepaper)
author_source: Chris Stucchio, Visual Website Optimizer (VWO), whitepaper PDF, ca. 2015
note: Technical explanation of Beta-Binomial Bayesian testing, expected loss and decision rules as implemented in a commercial CRO tool; the PyMC Bayesian A/B notebook implements these models.
course_use: Reading for the Bayesian A/B session; pair with PyMC notebook. Free.

title: CXL: A/B Testing Statistics - An Easy-to-Understand Guide
author_source: CXL (ConversionXL), cxl.com blog/guide
note: Marketer-friendly explanation of mean, variance, significance, confidence intervals and sample size for conversion tests; companion articles on 10 statistics traps and analysing test results. Includes the CRO rule of thumb of at least 1,000 conversions per month.
course_use: Accessible pre-reading for business students before the formal statistics; discuss rules of thumb critically. Free.

title: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) Checker
author_source: Lukas Vermeer (formerly Director of Experimentation, Booking.com), lukasvermeer.nl, web tool and Chrome extension
note: Enter observed counts per variant to test for SRM with a chi-squared test; site links to the KDD paper on automated SRM detection. SRM occurs in roughly 6-10% of experiments even at big tech firms.
course_use: Lab exercise: students check an SRM by hand in scipy and verify with the tool. Free.

title: Analytics-Toolkit.com: statistical tools for online A/B tests
author_source: Georgi Georgiev, Analytics-Toolkit.com, web tools (paid) with free calculators
note: Sequential (AGILE) test planning, power and sample-size calculators, non-binomial metric significance (e.g. average revenue per user). Companion book site abtestingstats.com.
course_use: Reference for sequential testing; some calculators free, full toolkit paid (subscription).

title: e-dialog Signifikanzrechner für A/B- und multivariate Tests
author_source: e-dialog (Vienna-based digital marketing agency), e-dialog.group, German-language tool and guide
note: Austrian agency tool for chi-squared significance across up to 8 variants; accompanying blog post explains the three calculation steps in German. Local practice link for a Vienna audience.
course_use: German-language resource; possible local guest-speaker link. Free (may require form).

title: Netflix Technology Blog: Decision Making at Netflix (multi-part series)
author_source: Martin Tingley et al., Netflix Technology Blog (Medium), 2021-2022, blog series (7 parts)
note: Accessible series: What is an A/B Test?, false positives and statistical significance, false negatives and power, building confidence in a decision, experimentation as a learning culture. Uses Netflix UI examples (artwork, rows) that students know.
course_use: Best non-technical intro series; assign parts 2-4 as weekly readings. Free.

title: Netflix Technology Blog: Sequential A/B Testing Keeps the World Streaming (Part 1: Continuous Data)
author_source: Netflix Technology Blog (Medium), 2024, blog post
note: How Netflix uses anytime-valid sequential tests for software rollouts; good follow-up to Evan Miller's peeking essay. Related Netflix posts: Quasi Experimentation at Netflix, Interleaving for personalisation, Heterogeneous Treatment Effects at Netflix.
course_use: Advanced reading on sequential testing. Free.

title: How Booking.com increases the power of online experiments with CUPED
author_source: Simon Jackson, Booking.com data science, booking.ai (Medium), 2018, blog post
note: Retail/travel example of CUPED: as products mature, effects shrink and pre-experiment covariates are needed to detect them; includes R code intuition. Booking.com is the canonical experimentation-culture company.
course_use: Reading for variance reduction; students reimplement CUPED in Python on simulated data. Free.

title: Spotify Engineering: Risk-Aware Product Decisions in A/B Tests with Multiple Metrics
author_source: Spotify Experimentation Platform team, engineering.atspotify.com, March 2024, blog post
note: How success, guardrail (non-inferiority), deterioration and quality metrics combine into one ship decision, with error-rate implications. Companion post: Choosing a Sequential Testing Framework (2023).
course_use: Discussion piece for the metrics and decision-rule session. Free.

title: Spotify Confidence blog (Experiment like Spotify series)
author_source: Spotify, confidence.spotify.com/blog, company blog 2023-2026
note: Posts on experiment analysis, experiments with smaller samples, and when proxy metrics break; practical, product-oriented.
course_use: Supplementary reading; small-sample post useful for marketers with low traffic. Free.

title: Beyond A/B Test: Speeding up Airbnb Search Ranking Experimentation through Interleaving
author_source: Qing Zhang, Michelle Du, Reid Andersen, Liwei He, The Airbnb Tech Blog (Medium), October 2022
note: Why low-frequency purchases (travel bookings) limit experiment bandwidth and how interleaving gave about 50x sensitivity for ranking tests. Good example of retail/marketplace constraints.
course_use: Case-style reading for the session on alternatives to classic A/B tests. Free.

title: Zalando Engineering Blog: Experimentation Platform at Zalando, Part 1 - Evolution
author_source: Zalando Engineering, engineering.zalando.com, January 2021, blog post (tag page has further posts)
note: European fashion e-commerce: why Zalando built its own platform (Octopus), standardised randomisation and t-test analysis, internal A/B testing training. Related: Marketing A/B Testing at Zalando (location-based tests) and the open-source ExpAn Python library.
course_use: European retail example; good for IB students. Free.

title: Etsy Code as Craft: Experimentation category
author_source: Etsy Engineering, etsy.com/codeascraft, company blog 2014-2024
note: Marketplace experimentation posts: How Etsy Handles Peeking in A/B Testing, Imbalance Detection, Double-bucketing, Control Variates for accuracy and speed, Interleaving, experiments with new visitors, collective impact of experiments.
course_use: Pick-and-choose readings; peeking post pairs with Evan Miller. Free.

title: Under the Hood of Uber's Experimentation Platform
author_source: Uber Engineering Blog, uber.com/blog, 2018, blog post
note: Covers A/B/N tests, causal inference and multi-armed bandits for marketing campaigns and promotions; classifies metrics into proportion, continuous and ratio metrics (ratio metrics need delta method).
course_use: Overview reading on platform architecture and metric types. Free.

title: Analytics-Toolkit Blog (Georgi Georgiev)
author_source: Georgi Georgiev, blog.analytics-toolkit.com, blog 2017-2026
note: Rigorous yet marketer-oriented posts: significance for non-binomial metrics (ARPU, AOV), one- vs two-tailed tests, sequential testing Q&A, interpretation mistakes. Author of Statistical Methods in Online A/B Testing.
course_use: Advanced readings for statistically keen students. Free.

title: Eppo blog: CUPED and CUPED++ - Bending time in experimentation
author_source: Eppo, geteppo.com/blog, 2023, company blog post (also Eppo Substack)
note: Intuitive explanation of CUPED as regression adjustment and how much runtime it can save; companion post Reducing Experiment Durations.
course_use: Intuition reading before the technical Microsoft deep dive. Free.

title: Statsig blog: A quick guide to sample ratio mismatch (SRM)
author_source: Statsig, statsig.com/blog, company blog post
note: What SRM is, how to detect it with a chi-squared test and common root causes (bots, redirects, logging). Statsig Perspectives hub has many short explainers (power, sample size).
course_use: Short reading for the data quality session. Free.

title: Understanding CUPED (with Python code)
author_source: Matteo Courthoud, personal blog / Towards Data Science, 2022, blog post with notebook on GitHub
note: Shows CUPED is a residualised outcome regression, compares with difference-in-differences and regression adjustment on simulated data; code in github.com/matteocourthoud/Blog-Posts. Same author: Bayesian AB Testing post on priors.
course_use: Python lab template for variance reduction. Free.

title: Bytepawn: A/B testing posts (Marton Trencseni)
author_source: Marton Trencseni, bytepawn.com, personal blog 2020-2025
note: Dozens of simulation-based Python posts: early stopping, five ways to reduce variance, CUPED and A/A false positives, A/B testing on social networks, review of the Gordon et al. advertising measurement paper (observational vs experimental lift).
course_use: Source of Monte Carlo exercises students can reproduce. Free.

title: The ultimate guide to A/B testing (Ronny Kohavi on Lenny's Newsletter/Podcast)
author_source: Lenny Rachitsky with Ronny Kohavi, Lenny's Newsletter, July 2023, newsletter post with transcript
note: Kohavi on when to start experimenting, building an experimentation culture, Twyman's law, typical success rates of ideas; transcript makes it citeable.
course_use: Reading or listening assignment; video version listed under tutorials. Free (some newsletter content paywalled).

title: konversionsKRAFT: Statistik und Analytics fuer A/B-Tests (Data Science Rubrik)
author_source: konversionsKRAFT (Web Arts AG), konversionskraft.de, German-language CRO blog
note: German articles on Konfidenz and Signifikanz, test power (70% of A/B tests are underpowered), test planning, Bayesian revenue/uplift evaluation and 10 Statistik-Fallen beim Testing; includes free calculators.
course_use: German-language readings for students who prefer German; good for practitioner perspective. Free.

title: A/B-Testing: Der grosse Starter-Guide
author_source: t3n, t3n.de, German-language article
note: German practitioner guide with four-step process: identify problem, research factors, form hypothesis, build variant. Good for the hypothesis-design part, weak on statistics.
course_use: Short German warm-up reading; let students critique missing statistical planning. Free.

title: e-dialog Blog: Wann ist Ihr Testergebnis signifikant? Die Statistik hinter dem A/B-Test
author_source: e-dialog (Vienna), e-dialog.group/blog, German-language blog post
note: Austrian agency explains the chi-squared significance calculation in three steps (critical value 3.84 at 95%); note the common but imprecise interpretation of confidence, useful for a misconception discussion.
course_use: German reading; ask students to spot the p-value misinterpretation. Free.

title: A/B-Test: Wie berechne ich Stichproben und Testdauer?
author_source: Kameleoon, kameleoon.com/de/blog, German-language blog post
note: German explanation of sample size and test duration planning by a European A/B testing vendor; complements AB Tasty German post on statistische Signifikanz.
course_use: German supplementary reading for the planning session. Free.

title: AB Tasty Blog: Which Statistical Model is Best for A/B Testing - Bayesian, Frequentist, CUPED, or Sequential?
author_source: AB Tasty, abtasty.com/blog, company blog post
note: Vendor comparison of four analysis approaches; useful to show vendor framing (AB Tasty prefers Bayesian). German version of the significance article at abtasty.com/de/blog/statistische-signifikanz-a-b-tests/.
course_use: Critical reading: compare vendor claims with Kohavi/Georgiev. Free.

title: Experiment Nation (newsletter and podcast)
author_source: Rommil Santiago, Experiment Nation, Substack and podcast, ongoing
note: Community newsletter and podcast with interviews of CRO and experimentation practitioners; episode 47 features Ronny Kohavi on statistics concepts experimenters must know.
course_use: Optional listening; source of potential guest speakers. Free.

title: A/B Testing (Introduction to A/B Testing) by Google
author_source: Carrie Grimes, Caroline Buckey, Diane Tang (Google), Udacity, MOOC, ca. 21 hours, beginner-intermediate
note: Five lessons: overview, policy and ethics, choosing and characterising metrics, designing an experiment (sizing, MDE), analysing results; final project with data. Still the most-cited free course; lesson 2 on ethics is rare elsewhere.
course_use: Self-study companion; assign lessons 3-5 before the corresponding sessions. Free (Udacity login).

title: A/B Testing in Python
author_source: Moe Lotfy, DataCamp, interactive course, 4 hours, intermediate
note: Four chapters: overview and metrics, design and planning (power, MDE, sample size), data processing, sanity checks and analysis of proportions, means and non-parametric tests; uses statsmodels, scipy and pingouin. Close match to a Python-based business course.
course_use: Homework track; DataCamp for the Classroom gives free access for instructors and students. Otherwise paid subscription (~USD 25/month).

title: Customer Analytics and A/B Testing in Python
author_source: DataCamp, interactive course, ca. 4 hours
note: Combines KPI/customer analytics with A/B test design and analysis on a subscription-app case; good marketing framing.
course_use: Alternative DataCamp track; DataCamp Classroom free for teaching, else paid.

title: Accelerating Innovation with A/B Testing
author_source: Ronny Kohavi, Maven, live cohort course, 5 sessions x 2-2.5 hours over 2 weeks, practitioner level
note: The leading practitioner course: concepts, culture, trust, pitfalls with examples from Amazon, Microsoft, Airbnb; 30+ cohorts. Not for students but ideal instructor upskilling.
course_use: Instructor preparation; paid (several hundred to ca. USD 2,000 per seat, check current price on Maven).

title: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)
author_source: Lenny's Podcast, YouTube, 2023, video interview ca. 1.5 hours
note: Wide-ranging interview: experimentation culture, OEC, Twyman's law, failure rates of ideas, institutional memory. Transcript on lennysnewsletter.com for picking segments.
course_use: Clip segments for the opening session; full episode as optional viewing. Free.

title: A/B Testing Statistics Concepts Experimenters must know with Ronny Kohavi
author_source: Experiment Nation, YouTube, video talk/interview
note: Kohavi on p-value misinterpretation, false positive risk, power, SRM and variance reduction; statistics-focused complement to the Lenny interview.
course_use: Video for the inference session. Free.

title: Ronny Kohavi YouTube channel
author_source: Ronny Kohavi, YouTube channel
note: Collects Kohavi's talks and course trailers; his talks page robotics.stanford.edu/~ronnyk/ronnyk-talks.html lists slide decks such as Pitfalls in Online Controlled Experiments (CODE@MIT 2016) and Metric Pitfalls (CODE@MIT 2017).
course_use: Browse for talks to embed. Free.

title: Statistical Power, Clearly Explained!!!
author_source: Josh Starmer, StatQuest, YouTube, ca. 8 minutes, beginner
note: Visual explanation of power via overlapping distributions; follow-up video Power Analysis, Clearly Explained. StatQuest p-value videos also fit.
course_use: Flipped-classroom video before the sample-size lab. Free.

title: A/B Testing in Data Science (playlist)
author_source: Emma Ding, Data Interview Pro, YouTube playlist, multiple videos 10-25 minutes, intermediate
note: Interview-oriented but compact explanations of experiment design, metrics, sample size, novelty and network effects, common analysis mistakes. Key video: Crack A/B Testing Problems for Data Science Interviews (youtube.com/watch?v=X8u6kr4fxXc).
course_use: Review material before exams; motivates students with career relevance. Free.

title: A/B Testing Course: A/B Test like a Pro! (full course)
author_source: Tomi Mester, Data36, YouTube playlist, 2021, 37 videos ca. 3 hours, beginner
note: Free beginner course from an online-business perspective: success metrics, hypotheses, test design, evaluation; course site data36.com/ab-testing-course-ab-test-like-a-pro/ has materials.
course_use: Entry-level self-study for students without statistics background. Free.

title: Easy as ABC: A Quick Introduction to Bayesian A/B Testing in Python
author_source: Will Barker, YouTube, conference talk, beginner-intermediate
note: Beta-Binomial Bayesian A/B testing in Python with probability-to-beat-control; good bridge to the PyMC notebook.
course_use: Video for the Bayesian session. Free.

title: Usable A/B testing - A Bayesian approach (PyData Berlin 2016)
author_source: PyData Berlin 2016, PyVideo, conference talk recording
note: Why conventional results are hard to interpret for stakeholders and a visual Bayesian alternative; Berlin e-commerce context.
course_use: Optional video for Bayesian A/B. Free.

title: Introduction to Bayesian A/B Testing (PyMC example notebook)
author_source: PyMC developers (Cuong Duong), PyMC example gallery, 2021, Jupyter notebook
note: Implements the VWO whitepaper models: Beta-Binomial conversion model, prior predictive checks, revenue model, multi-variant tests, with code.
course_use: Lab notebook for the Bayesian session (students run in Colab). Free, open source.

title: CausalML documentation and example notebooks (uplift modelling, meta-learners)
author_source: Uber, causalml.readthedocs.io, Python package documentation with notebooks
note: Notebooks on S/T/X/R-learners, uplift trees, uplift curves and validation with TMLE; shows how experiment data feed targeting decisions (who to send a coupon to). Related talk: Juan Camilo Orduz, Introduction to Uplift Modeling, PyConDE and PyData Berlin 2022 (juanitorduz.github.io/uplift/).
course_use: Advanced lab: from average treatment effect to targeted marketing. Free, open source.

title: CODE@MIT 2024 (Conference on Digital Experimentation) - YouTube playlist
author_source: MIT Initiative on the Digital Economy, YouTube playlist, 2024 conference recordings
note: Research and industry talks on digital experimentation (interference, marketplaces, advertising lift, adaptive experiments). Earlier years on ide.mit.edu event pages; 2019 fireside chat at youtube.com/watch?v=gfXlpdnFlmM.
course_use: Pick one academic talk for a research-oriented session or thesis students. Free.

title: A/B Testing in a Marketing Campaign (Python) - Kaggle notebook
author_source: Kaggle community notebook (seanlayer), uses Kaggle Marketing A/B Testing dataset
note: Worked analysis of an ad vs PSA marketing experiment with conversion tests; Kaggle also hosts Cookie Cats retention A/B notebooks. Quality varies, useful as critique material.
course_use: Lab starter; ask students to find and fix analysis weaknesses (e.g. no power analysis, SRM). Free (Kaggle login to run).

title: The Math Behind A/B Testing with Example Python Code
author_source: Nguyen Ngo, Towards Data Science (Medium), 2018, written tutorial with code
note: Classic tutorial deriving the two-proportion z-test, power and sample size from Bernoulli/binomial and CLT with plotting code; very close to what a stats-for-business lab needs.
course_use: Lab handout basis. Free (Medium metered paywall possible).

title: Run Smart A/B Tests (Coursera short course)
author_source: Coursera, short course for marketing professionals, beginner
note: Email-marketing focused A/B testing: hypothesis-driven design, test parameters, analysis. Light on statistics but squarely in marketing practice.
course_use: Optional marketing-practice module; audit free, certificate paid.

title: A/B-Testing im Online-Shop (Webinar)
author_source: conversionboosting, conversionboosting.com, German-language webinar recording
note: German e-commerce webinar on running A/B tests in online shops; same site has a Leitfaden for A/B tests on product detail pages.
course_use: German practitioner input for the retail application session. Free (registration may be required).

title: Booking.com
author_source: Stefan Thomke and Daniela Beyersdorfer, Harvard Business School Case 619-015, October 2018, case, 28 pages; Teaching Note 620-080 (2020); distributed via HBP and The Case Centre
note: Flagship teaching case on large-scale online experimentation: how Booking.com runs thousands of concurrent A/B tests, democratised testing (about 75 percent of core staff can launch tests), failure rates of experiments, culture and governance vs. design intuition. Good for discussing experimentation culture, guardrail metrics and when not to test. Teaching note exists (620-080). No dataset.
course_use: Opening case discussion for the experimentation block; pair with Kohavi/Thomke HBR 2017 and the HBR IdeaCast 'At Booking.com, Innovation Means Constant Failure'. Paid, HBP educator account, approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren. Also listed at The Case Centre: https://www.thecasecentre.org/products/view?id=157117

title: Experimentation at Yelp
author_source: Iavor Bojinov and Karim R. Lakhani, Harvard Business School Case 621-064, October 2020 (revised March 2024), case, 20 pages
note: Yelp's path from ad-hoc team tests to a central experimentation platform, plus a pivotal experiment on geographically constrained ads with a trade-off between user experience and revenue that the protagonist must resolve. Good for metric choice (OEC vs. guardrails), platform build vs. buy, and decision-making under conflicting results.
course_use: Case discussion after the basics of A/B testing; decision question works well as a vote at the start of class. Paid, HBP educator account, approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren; teaching note availability check on HBP.

title: Orchadio's First Two Split Experiments
author_source: Iavor Bojinov, Marco Iansiti and David Lane, Harvard Business School Case 622-015, August 2021, case
note: Direct-to-consumer grocery e-commerce firm plans its first two A/B tests: a redesigned website (functionality and effectiveness) and four banner variants. Uses feature flags (Split platform). Managers must decide test design and whether/how to sequence the experiments. Very close to a typical retail/marketing setting; good for hypothesis, metrics, sample size, interaction of concurrent tests.
course_use: Beginner-friendly case for designing an A/B test before any statistics; students draft an experiment plan in groups. Paid, HBP, approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Innovation at Uber: The Launch of Express POOL
author_source: Chiara Farronato, Alan D. MacCormack and Sarah Mehta, Harvard Business School Case 619-003, 2018, case
note: Describes a five-week synthetic control experiment (Feb 2018, six US cities) testing an extension of the matching window from two to five minutes: 5.2 percent more double matches, 7.4 percent fewer single matches. Shows why simple user-level A/B tests fail in two-sided marketplaces (interference) and how city-level or synthetic control designs help; efficiency vs. customer experience trade-off.
course_use: Advanced session on experiments beyond simple A/B (interference, switchbacks, synthetic controls). Paid, HBP/Case Centre, approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: A/B Testing at Vungle
author_source: Yael Grushka-Cockayne, Kenneth C. Lichtendahl Jr. (Darden), Bert De Reyck and Ioannis Fragkos (UCL), Darden Business Publishing UVA-QA-0821, 2015, case; teaching note UVA-QA-0821TN (5 pages)
note: Two recent MBA graduates built a new ad-serving algorithm for a mobile ad network that seems to beat the incumbent; students must evaluate the A/B 'horse race' with hypothesis tests on profitability. Written explicitly for a course covering hypothesis testing, so it maps directly onto a quantitative A/B testing lesson. Teaching note available; check for student spreadsheet.
course_use: Lab case: students replicate the test in Python (two-proportion test, revenue per impression). Paid, Darden Business Publishing or The Case Centre (https://www.thecasecentre.org/products/view?id=127736); per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Advertising Experiments at the Ohio Art Company
author_source: Rajkumar Venkatesan and Paul W. Farris, Darden Business Publishing UVA-M-0752, 2007, case with student spreadsheet and teaching note
note: Two real advertising field experiments of a toy maker (Etch A Sketch) with retailer partners; discusses measuring return on marketing and the biases that threaten causal inference in field experiments (non-random markets, confounding, spillover). Student spreadsheet included, so it doubles as a data exercise on offline/retail experiments.
course_use: Bridge from online A/B tests to retail/advertising field experiments; spreadsheet can be analysed in Python. Paid, Darden or The Case Centre (https://www.thecasecentre.org/products/view?id=83359); per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Designing Marketing Experiments (technical note)
author_source: Rajkumar Venkatesan, Darden Business Publishing UVA-M-0839, August 2012, technical note
note: Short technical note used in Darden's core marketing and marketing analytics courses: test and control design, randomisation, measuring lift. Designed to pair with the Ohio Art case.
course_use: Pre-reading for business students before the first experiment case. Paid, Darden; per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Winning an Election (Obama 2008 splash page experiment)
author_source: Vishal Gupta, USC Marshall School of Business, BUAD 425 course case, PDF, year not stated
note: Free short classroom case built on the Obama 2008 campaign's multivariate test of the donation splash page (4 buttons x 6 media, 310,382 visitors). Lets students analyse a factorial A/B/n test and compute the business value of the winner.
course_use: Free warm-up or homework case; works with Python for multiple-comparison discussion. Free PDF; check whether data are included.

title: Pilgrim Bank (A): Customer Profitability
author_source: Frances X. Frei and Dennis Campbell, Harvard Business School Case 602-104, October 2001 (revised October 2017), case with Excel dataset; sequels (B) Customer Retention and (C) Electronic Billpay
note: Classic data case: does online banking make customers more profitable? Data are observational, not randomised, so students meet selection bias and see why an experiment would be needed. Regression, sampling, profitability. Useful as the contrast case 'what if you cannot randomise'.
course_use: Python lab on observational vs. experimental evidence; follow with a discussion of how Pilgrim could design a field experiment. Paid, HBP approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: J.C. Penney's 'Fair and Square' Pricing Strategy
author_source: Elie Ofek and Jill Avery, Harvard Business School Case 513-036, September 2012 (revised January 2013), case; abridged version 514-063; supplements (B) and (C)
note: CEO Ron Johnson's rollout of everyday low pricing without prior market tests; sales collapsed. The famous quote that Apple did not test is the hook for discussing why pricing changes should be piloted in test stores or online price experiments. Strategy case, no dataset.
course_use: Motivational case on 'the cost of not testing'; ask students to design the test JCPenney should have run (store-level randomisation, duration, metrics). Paid, HBP approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Building an e-Commerce Brand at Wayfair
author_source: Thales S. Teixeira and Elizabeth Anne Watkins, Harvard Business School Case 516-028, August 2015, case
note: Online furniture retailer decides on its advertising budget (TV brand advertising vs. performance marketing) and on how to measure its effect. Useful entry point to incrementality and why attribution data mislead; experiment design is a discussion extension rather than the case's main content.
course_use: Case discussion on advertising measurement; extension task: design a geo or holdout test for Wayfair's TV campaign. Paid, HBP approx. USD 5 per student copy; per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Marketplace Tutorial: Price Elasticity in Practice
author_source: Harvard Business Publishing Education, product MP0035-HTM-ENG, interactive tutorial; also in Marketplace Tutorial Bundle: Pricing (MP0059)
note: Interactive exercise in which students run a pricing experiment and use the experiment data to estimate price elasticity of demand. A safe environment to practise price tests before discussing real price experiments.
course_use: In-class or homework exercise for the price-experiment session. Paid, HBP per student licence; per Kurs zu lizenzieren.

title: Udacity A/B Testing (by Google): Final Project 'Free Trial Screener'
author_source: Udacity in collaboration with Google, free online course (ud257), final project with real experiment data
note: Real Udacity experiment: after clicking 'start free trial', users were asked how many hours they can study; under 5 hours they were nudged to the free materials. Students choose invariant and evaluation metrics, compute variability, sample size and duration, run sanity checks and sign tests, and make a launch decision. Many worked solutions on GitHub and Medium for instructor reference.
course_use: Complete free lab or graded project in Python; ideal end-to-end exercise for business students. Free.

title: Cookie Cats mobile game A/B test (gate 30 vs. gate 40)
author_source: Tactile Entertainment data, originally a DataCamp project, Kaggle dataset; many public GitHub analyses
note: 90,189 players randomised to gate_30 or gate_40; variables sum_gamerounds, retention_1, retention_7. Moving the gate to level 40 lowered 7-day retention from 19.0 to 18.2 percent (significant), so the change should not ship. Great for proportions tests, bootstrap, outliers in engagement data and the 'counter-intuitive result' discussion.
course_use: First Python lab on A/B test analysis (60-90 min); exam-style question possible. Free; Kaggle login for download.

title: Marketing A/B Testing dataset (ad vs. PSA)
author_source: Favio Vazquez, Kaggle dataset, open
note: 588,101 users, 96 percent saw the ad and 4 percent a public service announcement (holdout control); variables converted, total_ads, most_ads_day, most_ads_hour. Ad group converts 2.55 vs. 1.79 percent (about 43 percent relative lift). Good for holdout/incrementality logic, unbalanced allocation and dose-response pitfalls (total_ads is post-treatment).
course_use: Python lab on incrementality testing; discussion question: is the ad worth its cost? Free; Kaggle login.

title: Advanced A/B Testing Workshop (Marketing Analytics Summit 2019)
author_source: Elea McDonnell Feit (Drexel), GitHub repository eleafeit/ab_test, workshop materials with code and data
note: Hands-on workshop on analysing marketing experiments (email/website tests), heterogeneous effects and test planning, by a leading marketing experiments researcher. Code is R, but data and logic port easily to Python. Related: Test & Roll replication files (github.com/eleafeit/testandroll) for profit-maximising test sizes.
course_use: Instructor material and lab template; students translate one notebook to Python. Free.

title: HBS publications search: A/B testing (case finder)
author_source: Harvard Business School Faculty & Research, publications filtered by keyword 'A/b Testing'
note: Running list of HBS cases, notes and articles tagged A/B testing; useful to check for newer experimentation cases (e.g. by Bojinov, Thomke, Farronato) before each semester.
course_use: Instructor tool for case selection; then buy via HBP. Free to browse.

title: Bing ad headline test: 12 percent revenue, over USD 100 million per year
author_source: Ron Kohavi and Stefan Thomke, 'The Surprising Power of Online Experiments', Harvard Business Review, Sept-Oct 2017 (reprint R1705E)
note: A shelved low-priority idea (lengthening ad title lines) was finally A/B tested and raised revenue by 12 percent, over USD 100M per year in the US, without hurting user-experience metrics; Bing's best revenue idea ever. Article also covers 10-25 percent annual revenue-per-search gains from many small tests, and the low success rate of ideas. Free reprint PDF via NYU Stern: https://web-docs.stern.nyu.edu/executive/The%20Surprising%20Power%20of%20Online%20Experiments.pdf
course_use: Warm-up story for session 1 and required reading. HBR paywall; WU-Lizenz prüfen (Business Source); free PDF copy exists.

title: Obama 2008 campaign: the USD 60 million splash page experiment
author_source: Dan Siroker (Director of Analytics, Obama 2008; later Optimizely co-founder), Optimizely blog
note: Full-factorial test of 4 buttons x 6 media (Google Website Optimizer), 310,382 visitors, about 13,000 per cell. 'Learn More' button plus family photo: 11.6 vs. 8.26 percent sign-up (+40.6 percent). Extrapolated to 2.88M extra emails, 288,000 volunteers and USD 60M donations. Lesson: videos the staff loved performed worst.
course_use: Warm-up and calculation exercise (back out the value per email). Free.

title: Facebook ad lift studies vs. observational methods
