author_source: Brett R. Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava and Dan Chapsky, 'A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook', Marketing Science 38(2), 193-225, 2019
note: 12 US Facebook conversion lift RCTs (435M user-study observations, 1.4B impressions) compared with exposed vs. unexposed, matching, regression adjustment, matched-market and before-after estimates; observational methods often miss the experimental lift, sometimes by a factor of three, even with thousands of covariates. Free Kellogg white paper version available.
course_use: Reading for the advertising measurement session; table of estimates is a strong exam discussion item. Journal paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen; free white paper at kellogg.northwestern.edu.

title: Where A/B testing goes wrong: divergent delivery in ad platform tests
author_source: Michael Braun and Eric M. Schwartz, Journal of Marketing, 2025
note: Shows that A/B tests run inside Meta/Google ad tools deliver each ad to differently optimised audiences, so the comparison is not randomised between creatives; what such tests can and cannot tell marketers. Very relevant pitfall for students who will use platform 'experiments'.
course_use: Pitfalls session; short in-class reading of the managerial summary. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Artwork Personalization at Netflix
author_source: Netflix Technology Blog, 2017
note: Netflix tests and personalises title artwork per member using contextual bandits after classic A/B tests showed artwork drives viewing choices; rolled out to 130M+ members, most helpful for lesser-known titles. Bridges A/B tests to bandits and personalisation; good discussion of metrics (take rate vs. watch time).
course_use: Example for creative testing and the step from A/B to bandits. Free.

title: Experiments at Airbnb (price filter test and peeking)
author_source: Airbnb Engineering and Data Science blog (Jan Overgoor), nerds.airbnb.com, about 2014; follow-ups 'Experiment Reporting Framework' and 'Scaling Airbnb's Experimentation Platform' on Medium
note: Test raising the search price filter maximum from USD 300 to 1000; shows how p-values cross the 0.05 line early and then drift back (peeking), why to wait for convergence, and how to segment results by browser to detect bugs. Ideal pitfall illustration with real plots.
course_use: Pitfalls session (peeking, novelty, segment bugs); pair with a Python simulation of repeated significance testing. Free.

title: Avoid the Pitfalls of A/B Testing (LinkedIn and Netflix)
author_source: Iavor Bojinov, Guillaume Saint-Jacques and Martin Tingley, Harvard Business Review 98(2), 48-53, March-April 2020
note: Three practitioner pitfalls with LinkedIn and Netflix examples: averages hide segment effects (heterogeneity), network interference between connected customers, and short tests missing changing reactions over time (novelty/primacy).
course_use: Short reading for pitfalls session. HBR paywall; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: OkCupid: 'We Experiment On Human Beings!'
author_source: Christian Rudder, OkCupid OkTrends blog, July 2014; coverage by Forbes (Kashmir Hill) and TIME
note: Dating site told poorly matched pairs they were a 90 percent match (and vice versa) to test the power of suggestion; also 'Love is Blind' day without photos. Rudder argued every website experiments on users. Strong contrast for consent, deception and the business-research boundary.
course_use: Ethics discussion (10-15 minutes), possibly a role play with the Facebook case. Free.

title: Experimentation Platform at Zalando: Part 1 - Evolution (Octopus)
author_source: Zalando Engineering Blog, January 2021
note: How Europe's largest online fashion retailer (Berlin) moved from team-by-team manual tests to the central platform Octopus (2015), with standardised randomisation and two-sided t-tests at 5 percent; links to the open-source Python library ExpAn. Close-to-home DACH retail example.
course_use: Example for the 'experimentation organisation' session; ExpAn can be shown in the Python lab. Free.

title: Marketing A/B Testing at Zalando: location-based tests for marketing
author_source: Zalando data scientists, Towards Data Science (Medium)
note: Why user-level randomisation does not work for many marketing channels and how Zalando uses location (geo) based A/B tests to measure marketing incrementality. Good link between online A/B tests and geo experiments for campaigns.
course_use: Reading for the advertising incrementality session. Free (Medium metered).

title: A/B testing at Zalando: concepts and tools (PyData Berlin 2018)
author_source: Shan Huang and Grigory Bordyugov, Zalando, PyData Berlin 2018 talk, YouTube recording
note: Practitioner talk on concepts (metrics, power, sequential testing) and the Python tools used at Zalando; good bridge to a Python-based course.
course_use: Optional video for students; excerpt in class. Free.

title: Is A/B testing effective? Evidence from 35,000 startups
author_source: Rembrand Koning, Sharique Hasan and Aaron Chatterji, 'Experimentation and Start-up Performance: Evidence from A/B Testing', Management Science 68(9), 6434-6453, 2022; HBS Working Knowledge summary
note: Panel of 35,262 startups (2015-2019): adopters of A/B testing tools see 30 to 100 percent performance gains after a year and both scale and fail faster. Evidence for the business value of experimentation, plus a nice discussion of how the authors identify a causal effect without an experiment.
course_use: Short reading on the value of experimentation; meta-discussion of methods. Summary free; journal WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Lessons from More Than 1,000 E-Commerce Pricing Tests
author_source: Harvard Business Review, March 2024, article
note: Practitioner synthesis of over 1,000 online price tests: what price experiments typically find and how to run them. Search snippet confirms title and date only; check authors and content before use.
course_use: Reading for a price experiments session. HBR paywall; WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Experimentation in marketplaces: switchbacks at Uber, Lyft and DoorDash (lecture slides)
author_source: Nikhil Garg, Cornell ORIE 5355 Lecture 14 'Experimentation in marketplaces', Fall 2022; Bojinov, Simchi-Levi and Zhao, 'Design and Analysis of Switchback Experiments' (arXiv 2009.00148)
note: Why user-level A/B tests are biased in two-sided marketplaces (pricing, matching) and how time-and-region switchback designs (e.g. Uber switching every ~160 minutes per city) fix it. Complements the Uber Express POOL case.
course_use: Advanced extension; slides as instructor background. Free.

title: The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising
author_source: Randall A. Lewis and Justin M. Rao, Quarterly Journal of Economics 130(4), 2015
note: 25 large field experiments with US retailers on Yahoo! show that ad effects are tiny relative to sales noise, so even experiments with millions of users can barely detect profitable campaigns. Excellent for power and minimum detectable effect discussions in a retail setting.
course_use: Power analysis session; students reproduce an MDE calculation in Python. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen. Link from memory, not checked in this run.

title: An Assortmentwide Decision-Support System for Dynamic Pricing and Promotion Planning in DIY Retailing (bauMax)
author_source: Natter, Reutterer, Mild and Taudes (WU Wien), Marketing Science 26(4), 576-583, 2007, article / ISMS Practice Prize 2005; Österreich
note: Austrian DIY retailer bauMax: weekly demand model (price, reference price, seasonality, features, discounts, cross-item effects) drives price and promotion decisions. Eight pricing rounds with thousands of SKUs served as testing ground, evaluated against several benchmarks; reported gross profit +8.1 percent and sales +2.1 percent. Lesson: price/promotion testing in brick-and-mortar retail is quasi-experimental (rounds, benchmarks, holdouts) rather than a clean A/B split; good contrast to online A/B tests. WU authors, so strong local hook.
course_use: Case discussion on offline price experiments vs. online A/B tests; ask students how they would design a cleaner store-level test (matched stores, holdout SKUs). Article paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: bauMax - ISMS Practice Prize 2005 video (dynamic pricing and promotion planning)
author_source: Natter, Reutterer, Mild, Taudes with bauMax, ISMS/Lilien Practice Prize video archive, 2005, video case; Österreich
note: Recorded practice-prize presentation of the bauMax pricing system: how model-based price changes were rolled out in rounds and evaluated against benchmarks inside an Austrian retailer; also on YouTube (BauMax - 2005 ISMS Practice Prize). Lesson: organisational side of testing (getting management to accept test rounds, measuring profit not just sales).
course_use: Video case (approx. 20-30 min) before discussing the Marketing Science paper; teaching-case substitute with Austrian context; possible guest-talk lead via WU (Reutterer). Free.

title: A dynamic segmentation approach for targeting and customizing direct marketing campaigns
author_source: Reutterer, Mild, Natter and Taudes (WU Wien), Journal of Interactive Marketing 20(3-4), 2006, article; Österreich
note: Controlled field experiment with several thousand loyalty-program members of a do-it-yourself retailer (Austrian research team; retailer presumably bauMax, not confirmed in snippet): segment-specific tailored direct-mail campaigns vs. control group; significant positive impact on sales and profitability. Lesson: test vs. control design for CRM/direct-mail campaigns, measuring incremental profit of personalisation.
course_use: Reading for the session on email/direct-mail and personalisation tests; students identify treatment, control, unit of randomisation, KPI. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: A/B testing to improve recommender products (willhaben real-time recommender)
author_source: Adevinta Tech Blog (Medium), ca. 2021-2022, company blog; willhaben, Österreich
note: willhaben (Austria's largest classifieds marketplace, Adevinta group) replaced an offline batch user-based recommender suffering from cold start with an online recommender built on real-time user profiles; the switch was validated with an A/B test of reactiveness to recent user interactions. Post also covers metric choice for recommender tests. Exact effect sizes for willhaben not in the snippet; check the post. Lesson: A/B tests for algorithm changes, choosing engagement vs. conversion metrics.
course_use: Warm-up: Austrian marketplace students know; guest-talk lead (willhaben data/product team, Vienna). Free.

title: Runtastic: user review on the paywall instead of promo copy (+44 percent paid subscriptions)
author_source: abtest.design (test library) and Designfolio Substack, undated, secondary write-up; Runtastic / adidas Running, Pasching/Linz, Österreich
note: Runtastic replaced the promotional statement on its in-app premium paywall with a real user review plus 5-star rating (social proof); reported +44 percent paid subscriptions. Evidence thin: secondary sources only, no sample size, duration or significance reported. Lesson: social proof on paywalls, but also a good critical-reading exercise (what is missing to trust a +44 percent claim?).
course_use: Warm-up or critique exercise on reported uplifts; Austrian app brand. Free.

title: Kleine Zeitung tackles branding, ad and subscription sales in a single campaign
author_source: INMA blog (International News Media Association), ca. 2019-2020, practitioner article; Kleine Zeitung, Styria Media Group, Graz, Österreich
note: Launch campaign for the digital subscription Kleine Web + App. Banner tests on website and Facebook varied price communication (per week vs. per month vs. no price), colours, fact- vs. image-based copy, CTA wording and button design: simple static fact-based banners beat animated ones, and a banner without price beat banners with price. Also reports brand-tracking uplift (aided recall 27 percent). Sample sizes not in snippet. Lesson: creative/message testing in an Austrian publisher, price framing in ads.
course_use: Short case discussion: students predict which banner wins before revealing results. INMA posts may need free registration.

title: How A1 Telekom Austria is using AI to unlock more customer value
author_source: BCG / BCG X, client story, ca. 2023-2024, consultancy case; A1 Telekom Austria, Österreich
note: BCG X built cross-/upsell propensity models and next-best-action targeting for A1 within 16 weeks, with an agile, experimental way of working across channels; reports up to 40 percent higher sales conversion in campaigns. Evidence thin on design: consultancy marketing piece, test/control set-up not documented. Lesson: personalisation in telco CRM and why uplift claims need a holdout group.
course_use: Discussion prompt: what experiment would you need to verify the 40 percent claim? Austrian telco context. Free.

title: Converting Online News Visitors to Subscribers: Exploring the Effectiveness of Paywall Strategies Using Behavioural Data
author_source: Xu, Thurman, Berhami, Strasser Ceballos and Fehling (LMU München / City St Georges), Journalism Studies, 2025, article (open access); Deutschland und Österreich
note: Behavioural data from 21 regional and local news sites (20 German, 1 Austrian): showing a standfirst below a paywalled headline cut the odds of clicking subscribe by 86.3 percent; higher price, paid trial and small gifts reduced subscription odds (4.5, 35.6, 14.0 percent); discounts and device bundles helped only for non-local visitors. Observational (cross-site variation), not randomised. Lesson: what A/B tests on paywall design should test, and why correlational evidence differs from experiments.
course_use: Reading plus contrast with Zeit Online/FAZ A/B tests: design an A/B test that would confirm the standfirst finding. Open access.

title: Onlinehändlerbefragung (ZHAW with Handelsverband Österreich), A/B-Testing usage among online retailers
author_source: ZHAW School of Management and Law with Handelsverband Österreich, Onlinehändlerbefragung 2022 (also 2021, 2023 A-CH editions), survey report; Österreich und Schweiz
note: Survey of Austrian and Swiss online retailers; per search snippet, about 15 percent of 509 respondents use a system for A/B or multivariate tests, and larger, more successful shops use them far more than small ones. Exact edition of the 15 percent figure not verified (may be 2021 or 2022). Lesson: diffusion of experimentation in DACH retail is low; motivates why SMEs do not test (traffic, skills).
course_use: Opening statistic for a lecture; discussion of barriers to A/B testing for small Austrian shops. Free PDF.

title: Dynamic Pricing for otto.de (A/B tests of pricing algorithms on article subgroups)
author_source: OTTO Tech Blog (Medium / otto.de techblog), ca. 2021, company blog; OTTO, Hamburg, Deutschland
note: OTTO evaluates dynamic-pricing algorithm changes by running versions on two or more homogeneous subgroups of articles in production (group A priced by algorithm X, group B by Y), with demand forecasts from OLS, XGBoost and LightGBM. Lesson: product-level (not user-level) randomisation for price tests, which avoids showing different customers different prices; discuss interference and fairness.
course_use: Case discussion on price experiments: why randomise products rather than customers? Free.

title: Learning to Rank: deep neural networks that learn to rank what you love (8-week A/B test on otto.de)
author_source: OTTO Tech Blog, ca. 2022-2023, company blog; OTTO, Hamburg, Deutschland
note: Neural ranking model for product search/listing tested for 8 weeks against the previous ranking: +1.86 percent clicks and +0.56 percent revenue, then rolled out to all users. Lesson: small relative lifts matter at scale; test duration, primary vs. secondary metrics.
course_use: Warm-up: is +0.56 percent revenue worth it? Compute absolute value with OTTO revenue. Free.

title: A story of experimentation culture at HelloFresh
author_source: HelloFresh Tech Blog (Medium), ca. 2019-2020, company blog; HelloFresh, Berlin, Deutschland
note: Experimentation platform team serving 30+ product teams from Berlin to Toronto; Optimizely chosen as single framework in 2018; won Optimizely Best Experimentation Program award. Related PyMC Labs post describes speeding HelloFresh's Bayesian A/B test pipeline from 5-6 hours to 5-6 minutes. Lesson: organisational scaling of experimentation in a Berlin subscription e-commerce firm.
course_use: Background reading on experimentation culture; guest-talk lead (HelloFresh experimentation team, Berlin). Free.

title: Creating a culture of experimentation at Delivery Hero (Vol. I) and the Fun with Flags platform
author_source: Delivery Hero Tech Blog, 2018 (plus later platform posts), company blog; Delivery Hero, Berlin, Deutschland
note: Product manager interview on building experimentation culture; related posts describe the in-house platform Fun with Flags (over 1 billion requests per week, used by about 90 percent of brands). No Delivery Hero switchback post found in search, so use DoorDash for switchbacks. Lesson: experimentation in a multi-brand delivery marketplace.
course_use: Background for a session on marketplace experiments; guest-talk lead. Free.

title: How Sequential Testing Accelerates Our Experimentation Velocity (Basemath)
author_source: GetYourGuide careers/tech blog (Konrad Richter et al.), ca. 2023-2024, company blog plus open-source repo; GetYourGuide, Zürich/Berlin, Schweiz und Deutschland
note: GetYourGuide developed its own sequential test (Basemath, open source on GitHub) to allow early stopping without inflating false positives; sibling posts cover clustered standard errors for ranking metrics and scaling A/B testing, and a PyData Berlin 2025 talk on democratising the platform. Lesson: peeking problem and sequential testing in a travel marketplace.
course_use: Methods session on peeking; students run the Basemath repo on simulated data. Free.

title: A/B Testing in action: Trivago case study (take-home analysis)
author_source: Nidhal (nidhalios), personal blog/GitHub, 2016, student-style case analysis; trivago, Düsseldorf, Deutschland
note: Worked analysis of a trivago A/B testing case task (data-based). trivago tech blog adds context: in-house C-test analytics app, example hypothesis of ranking hotels by city-centre distance vs. relevance, and a 2023 post on simulations to shorten A/B tests (tech.trivago.com). Evidence thin: unofficial write-up, verify data origin before class use.
course_use: Lab exercise template: students replicate the analysis; pair with trivago tech blog. Free.

title: Embeddings based complementary product recommendations at idealo (A/B test doubled engagement)
author_source: idealo Tech Blog (Medium), ca. 2021-2022, company blog; idealo, Berlin, Deutschland
note: Price-comparison site idealo built complementary-product recommendations without purchase data; online A/B test doubled user engagement with the module. Companion post on how to formulate A/B test hypotheses (medium.com/idealo-tech-blog/how-to-come-up-with-the-right-hypothesis-for-your-a-b-tests-dd5824967003). Lesson: offline vs. online metrics; hypothesis writing.
course_use: Hypothesis-writing exercise using the companion post. Free.

title: 4 learnings about subscription A/B testing from ZEIT ONLINE
author_source: The Audiencers (practitioner media), ca. 2022-2023, interview/article; ZEIT ONLINE, Hamburg/Berlin, Deutschland
note: Five years of paywall testing at ZEIT ONLINE: example test on which subscription benefits to promote; baseline conversion about 1.5 percent and target uplift 10 percent drive sample-size planning; alpha 5 or 10 percent depending on risk; one KPI per test to avoid false positives; complement with qualitative user tests. Lesson: realistic power calculation for low base rates.
course_use: Lab: compute required sample size for 1.5 percent baseline and 10 percent MDE. Free.

title: Dynamic paywall testing at Germany's FAZ
author_source: The Audiencers, 2024, practitioner article; also AVS/Medienhaus Next blog Warum A/B-Tests für die F.A.Z. unverzichtbar sind; Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Deutschland
note: FAZ ran 32 A/B tests in a year, 18 on the paywall; strikethrough reference prices lifted new-customer acquisition by 18 percent; first dynamic-paywall test (June 2024) used an in-house propensity-to-buy score: more paywalled content for highly engaged users gave +48 percent, about 20 extra orders per day. Lesson: price framing tests and targeting-based (heterogeneous treatment) paywalls; German-language companion post available.
course_use: Case discussion on reference prices and personalised paywalls; German source usable in German-taught courses. Free.

title: Bild's subscription testing drives its reader revenue plan
author_source: INMA Ideas blog, ca. 2019-2021, practitioner article; BILD / Axel Springer, Berlin, Deutschland
note: A/B tests on Bild's offer page showed more products and higher price points were not worth it; fewer products converted better; Bild then removed the offer page and placed the offer directly in the article; price increase first raised churn but paid off long-term. Numbers sparse in snippet. Lesson: choice overload, funnel friction, and short- vs. long-term metrics in price tests.
course_use: Discussion on long-term effects of price tests (churn). INMA may require free registration.

title: Case Study zu KPIs beim A/B-Testing: Conversion, Retouren, Deckungsbeitrag
author_source: konversionsKRAFT (Invesp/Web Arts), with BI partner nextel, undated, German agency case study; Deutschland
note: German fashion e-commerce test where the winning variant raised add-to-cart by 244 percent and orders through checkout by 43 percent, then examined whether returns eat up the uplift, measuring contribution margin instead of conversion. konversionsKRAFT also documents shoe retailer GÖRTZ (+5.7 percent revenue via value propositions; untested rollout could have cost up to -8.7 percent conversion). Agency sources, selective reporting likely. Lesson: choosing the right OEC in retail with high return rates.
course_use: German-language mini-case for the session on metrics/OEC; students argue conversion vs. margin. Free.

title: Personalized Online Advertising Effectiveness: The Interplay of What, When, and Where
author_source: Bleier and Eisenbeiss, Marketing Science 34(5), 669-688, 2015, article; field experiments with a large German fashion and sports retailer, Deutschland
note: Two large-scale field experiments plus two lab studies on retargeting banners: highly personalised banners work best right after a store visit but decay fast (overpersonalization); medium personalisation is more persistent; personalisation helps view-through only on motive-congruent sites. Lesson: personalisation tests need time and placement moderators; heterogeneity of treatment effects.
course_use: Reading for the personalisation/retargeting session. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Pay What You Want: A New Participative Pricing Mechanism
author_source: Kim, Natter and Spann (Frankfurt/LMU), Journal of Marketing 73(1), 44-58, 2009, article; field studies in Germany, Deutschland
note: Three field studies (restaurant buffet, cinema, delicatessen) in Germany: prices paid were well above zero; vs. regular prices, buffet payments were 19.4 percent lower, hot drinks at the deli 10.6 percent higher; PWYW can raise revenue. Design is before/after per outlet rather than randomised A/B. Lesson: price-mechanism field tests in retail and how to read non-randomised field evidence.
course_use: Classic reading for price experiments; class debate on design weaknesses. Article paywalled, preprint on ResearchGate, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Shipping fee schedules and return behavior
author_source: Lepthien and Clement (Universität Hamburg), Marketing Letters 30(2), 2019, article; randomized field experiment with an online shop, Deutschland
note: Shop visitors randomly assigned to one of seven shipping-fee schedules (minimum order values, flat fees, free-shipping thresholds). Shipping fees raised purchase value; threshold free shipping lowered purchase incidence and triggered strategic purchases that were returned later; minimum order values had no negative effect on purchases. Lesson: multi-arm price/promo field experiment, and why post-return metrics matter.
course_use: Reading plus exercise: design the seven-arm test and choose KPIs. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: From gut feeling to test culture (Vom Bauchgefühl zur Test-Kultur) incl. CO2 compensation checkout A/B test
author_source: Digitec Galaxus, company magazine article, ca. 2020-2021, company blog; Zürich, Schweiz
note: Switzerland's largest online retailer explains why it replaced an external testing tool with its own (page performance), and gives an example: two-week A/B test of a CO2-compensation option in checkout (A without, B with). Follow-up reports: about one in ten orders compensated, CHF 1.3 million in a year; under-30s compensate most (about 16 percent). Lesson: testing a sustainability feature for adoption and possible conversion side-effects.
course_use: Warm-up on testing non-revenue features (guardrail metrics: did checkout conversion drop?). German version on galaxus.de. Free.

title: The Cliffhanger Effect: how Blick's paywall strategy drives digital subscription growth
author_source: INMA Best Practice / INMA Ideas blog, 2024, practitioner article; Blick (Ringier), Zürich, Schweiz
note: Blick tested a Cliffhanger paywall (summary that stops at the key point) against a standard and a marketing-oriented paywall: +7 percent conversion vs. standard, +21 percent vs. marketing paywall on web. The Audiencers also covers Blick's Wheel of Luck gamified paywall experiment. Lesson: three-arm creative test on paywall copy in a Swiss tabloid.
course_use: Short case: students predict the ranking of the three paywalls. INMA best-practice pages may need login.

title: statsmodels (stats.proportion, stats.power, multipletests)
author_source: statsmodels developers, Python package, version 0.15.0 (PyPI, 27 Aug 2026), BSD-3-Clause, Python >=3.10
note: Workhorse for classical A/B analysis: proportions_ztest and confint_proportions_2indep for conversion rates, proportion_effectsize plus NormalIndPower / TTestIndPower for sample size and MDE, multipletests for Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg, OLS with covariates as regression adjustment (CUPED equivalent).
course_use: Core lab library for sessions 1-3 (test, power, multiple metrics). Open source (BSD-3), free.

title: SciPy (scipy.stats)
author_source: SciPy developers, Python package, version 1.18.1 (PyPI, 21 Aug 2026), BSD-3-Clause, Python >=3.12
note: ttest_ind(equal_var=False) for Welch tests on revenue per user, chisquare for the sample ratio mismatch check, chi2_contingency for multi-arm conversion tables, mannwhitneyu, scipy.stats.bootstrap and permutation_test for skewed basket values. Note: new version needs Python 3.12.
course_use: Lab: SRM check and Welch vs. bootstrap comparison on Hillstrom spend. Open source, free.

title: pingouin
author_source: Raphael Vallat, Python package, version 0.7.0 (PyPI, 26 Sep 2026), GPL-3.0, Python >=3.11
note: Student-friendly statistics API returning tidy DataFrames with effect size, CI, Bayes factor and achieved power in one call (ttest, anova, pairwise_tests, power_ttest). Good bridge for business students coming from SPSS-style output.
course_use: Warm-up lab for t-test and ANOVA on multi-arm promotion data (Fast Food dataset). Open source (GPL-3.0), free.

title: scikit-posthocs
author_source: Maksim Terpilovskii, Python package, version 0.17.0 (PyPI, 10 Sep 2026), MIT, Python >=3.9
note: Post-hoc pairwise comparisons (Tukey HSD, Dunn, Conover, Nemenyi) with p-value adjustment after an omnibus test on A/B/n tests with three or more arms.
course_use: Short demo in the multiple-testing session (three promotions in the Fast Food data). Open source (MIT), free.

title: spotify-confidence
author_source: Spotify, Python package, version 4.1.0 (PyPI, 26 Feb 2026), Apache-2.0, Python >=3.9
note: Industry library from Spotify's experimentation platform: z-tests and t-tests on summary statistics, sequential group tests with alpha spending, multiple-comparison correction, non-inferiority margins, built-in plots. Works on aggregated data, which mirrors how platforms compute results.
course_use: Lab on group sequential testing and guardrail (non-inferiority) metrics. Open source (Apache-2.0), free.

title: tea-tasting
author_source: Evgeny Ivanov (e10v), Python package, version 2.0.0 (PyPI, 7 Jun 2026), MIT, Python >=3.12
note: Modern A/B analysis package: Welch t-test, z-test, bootstrap, CUPED/CUPAC, delta method for ratio metrics (e.g. orders per session), SRM check, power analysis; computes statistics inside data backends via Ibis (DuckDB, BigQuery, Polars). Includes example data generator. Docs at tea-tasting.e10v.me.
course_use: Recommended main package for a full A/B lab notebook in Positron/Quarto (metrics, CUPED, ratio metrics). Open source (MIT), free.

title: Ambrosia
author_source: MTS AI (MobileTeleSystems), Python package, version 0.5.3.post1 (PyPI, 11 Jun 2026), Apache-2.0, Python 3.9-3.13
note: End-to-end experiment pipeline in three steps: Designer (sample size, MDE, duration from historical data), Splitter (hash-based and stratified group splits), Tester (t-test, bootstrap, multiple metrics). Shows the design side students rarely see.
course_use: Lab or project: design an experiment from historic retail data before running it. Open source (Apache-2.0), free; Python <3.14.

title: ExpAn (Zalando)
author_source: Zalando SE, Python package, version 1.4.0 (PyPI, 5 Jul 2019), MIT, no longer maintained
note: Historic e-commerce library from Zalando: delta method for ratio metrics, early-stopping and Bayesian variants. Unmaintained since 2019, so useful as reading code and for the history of retail experimentation, not as lab dependency.
course_use: Background only; point students to source code for delta-method implementation. Open source (MIT), free.

title: CausalML (Uber)
author_source: Uber Technologies, Python package, version 0.17.0 (PyPI, 4 Jul 2026), Apache-2.0, Python >=3.11
note: Uplift modelling and heterogeneous treatment effects: S/T/X/R/DR meta-learners, uplift trees and random forests, Qini and uplift curves, synthetic data generators (causalml.dataset). Directly matched to coupon and email targeting cases.
course_use: Lab on uplift targeting with Hillstrom or Criteo uplift data; student project. Open source (Apache-2.0), free.

title: EconML (Microsoft / PyWhy)
author_source: Microsoft Research ALICE / PyWhy, Python package, version 0.17.0 (PyPI, 31 Jul 2026), MIT, Python >=3.9
note: Double machine learning, causal forests (CausalForestDML), DR-learner and policy trees with confidence intervals for CATE; SHAP interpretation of who responds to a promotion. More inference-oriented than CausalML.
course_use: Advanced lab on heterogeneous treatment effects and targeting policies. Open source (MIT), free.

title: DoWhy (PyWhy)
author_source: PyWhy (originally Microsoft), Python package, version 0.14 (PyPI, 8 Nov 2025), MIT, Python 3.9-3.13
note: Four-step causal workflow (model, identify, estimate, refute) with DAGs; refutation tests (placebo treatment, random common cause). Good for contrasting experiments with observational marketing data; datasets.linear_dataset simulates data.
course_use: Demo in the quasi-experiments session: why randomisation removes the need for back-door adjustment. Open source (MIT), free.

title: scikit-uplift (sklift)
author_source: Maksim Shevchenko and contributors, Python package, version 0.5.1 (PyPI, 11 Aug 2022), MIT per repository
note: scikit-learn style uplift models (two-model, class transformation) and metrics (Qini AUC, uplift@k). Main value: one-line loaders fetch_hillstrom, fetch_criteo, fetch_x5, fetch_lenta, fetch_megafon for the standard marketing experiment datasets.
course_use: Data loader for labs; simple uplift baseline before CausalML. Open source, free; low maintenance since 2022, pin versions.

title: PyMC
author_source: PyMC developers, Python package, version 6.3.2 (PyPI, 8 Sep 2026), Apache-2.0, Python >=3.12
note: Probabilistic programming for Bayesian A/B tests: Beta-Binomial conversion models, hierarchical models across segments or markets, posterior probability to beat control and expected loss. PyMC example gallery has a Bayesian A/B testing introduction.
course_use: Lab on Bayesian A/B testing as contrast to frequentist tests. Open source (Apache-2.0), free.

title: Bambi
author_source: Bambi developers (PyMC ecosystem), Python package, version 0.21.0 (PyPI, 10 Sep 2026), MIT, Python >=3.12
note: Formula interface (like lme4/brms) on top of PyMC: Bayesian logistic regression of conversion on treatment plus covariates in one line. Lowers the coding barrier for business students.
course_use: Bayesian regression adjustment lab; compare with statsmodels logit. Open source (MIT), free.

title: PyMC-Marketing (lift-test calibration)
author_source: PyMC Labs, Python package, version 1.2.0 (PyPI, 29 Sep 2026), Apache-2.0, Python >=3.12
note: Bayesian media mix models that can be calibrated with results of geo or lift experiments (add_lift_test_measurements), linking incrementality tests to MMM; also CLV and customer choice modules.
course_use: Demo connecting experiments to marketing-mix modelling; capstone project. Open source (Apache-2.0), free.

title: tfcausalimpact (Python port of Google CausalImpact)
author_source: Willian Fuks, Python package, version 0.0.19 (PyPI, 20 Sep 2026), Apache-2.0, Python 3.8-3.13; based on Google's R package CausalImpact (Brodersen et al. 2015)
note: Bayesian structural time series counterfactual for a single treated series (one market, one campaign launch) with point and cumulative effect plots. Depends on TensorFlow Probability. The older pycausalimpact (0.1.1, 2020) is unmaintained.
course_use: Lab on quasi-experimental campaign evaluation when no randomisation is possible. Open source (Apache-2.0), free.

title: CausalImpact (R)
author_source: Google (Kay Brodersen, Alain Hauser), R package on CRAN, Apache-2.0
note: Original reference implementation of BSTS-based causal impact analysis with a very readable vignette; the standard tool in marketing analytics for campaign and pricing interventions.
course_use: Optional R comparison in Positron/Quarto. Open source, free. CRAN page not reachable from this session, check version.

title: GeoLift (Meta, R)
author_source: Meta Open Source (facebookincubator), R package on GitHub, MIT licence
note: End-to-end geo experimentation: market selection, power analysis by simulation, augmented synthetic control inference; walkthrough vignette with example data GeoLift_PreTest / GeoLift_Test; official tutorial for calling it from Python via rpy2.
course_use: Lab or project on geo lift tests for offline retail and post-cookie measurement. Open source (MIT), free; R install from GitHub.

title: GeoexperimentsResearch (Google, R)
author_source: Google, R package on GitHub, version 1.0.3, Apache-2.0
note: Implements geo-based regression (GBR) and time-based regression (TBR) for ROAS estimation from Vaver and Koehler; includes sample geo assignment and sales/cost data.
course_use: Background or advanced lab on geo experiments and iROAS. Open source, free.

title: trimmed_match and matched_markets (Google)
author_source: Google, Python libraries on GitHub (not on PyPI), Apache-2.0
note: trimmed_match: robust estimator of iROAS for paired geo experiments with outlier geos (Chen and Au 2022); matched_markets (github.com/google/matched_markets): designs and analyses matched-market experiments with TBR. Show how Google measures search ad incrementality.
course_use: Advanced demo for geo experiment design. Open source, free; installed from GitHub, notebooks in repos. Links not reachable from this session.

title: pysyncon
author_source: Stuart Lynn, Python package, version 1.7.0 (PyPI, 13 Sep 2026), MIT
note: Synthetic control in Python (standard, robust, augmented, penalised) with placebo tests; replicates Abadie's classic examples. Python alternative to GeoLift for market-level interventions.
course_use: Lab on synthetic control for a single-market campaign or store remodel. Open source (MIT), free.

title: MABWiser
author_source: Fidelity Investments AI Center of Excellence, Python package, version 2.7.4 (PyPI, 30 Aug 2024), Apache-2.0
note: Multi-armed and contextual bandits (epsilon-greedy, UCB, Thompson sampling, LinUCB) with simulation utilities; simple fit/predict API suitable for showing explore-exploit trade-offs against fixed-horizon A/B tests.
course_use: Lab: simulate a headline or banner test as A/B vs. Thompson sampling and compare regret. Open source (Apache-2.0), free.

title: Open Bandit Pipeline (obp)
author_source: ZOZO Research / Yuta Saito et al., Python package, version 0.5.7 (PyPI, 14 Apr 2023), Apache-2.0
note: Bandit policies and off-policy evaluation estimators (IPW, DR, DM) shipped with the Open Bandit Dataset from ZOZOTOWN fashion e-commerce; answers whether a new recommendation policy would beat the logged one without a new A/B test.
course_use: Advanced lab or thesis topic on off-policy evaluation. Open source (Apache-2.0), free; last release 2023.

title: Vowpal Wabbit
author_source: Vowpal Wabbit (originally Yahoo and Microsoft Research), Python package vowpalwabbit 9.11.9 (PyPI, 27 Sep 2026), BSD-3-Clause, Python >=3.10
note: Production-grade online learning and contextual bandits (used in Microsoft Personalizer); tutorials on simulating content personalisation with contextual bandits.
course_use: Demo of industrial contextual bandits; optional for advanced students. Open source (BSD-3), free.

title: GrowthBook
author_source: GrowthBook Inc., open source feature flagging and experimentation platform on GitHub (MIT core), Python SDK growthbook 3.2.0 (PyPI, 5 Oct 2026)
note: Warehouse-native platform with Bayesian (default), frequentist and sequential engines, CUPED, SRM detection, multiple-comparison corrections, bandits and power calculator; stats engine is open Python code (gbstats), so students can inspect what a commercial-grade tool computes.
course_use: Platform demo or self-hosted lab via Docker; cloud free tier for small teams. Open source (MIT core), free.

title: PostHog Experiments
author_source: PostHog Inc., product analytics with experiments; Python SDK posthog 7.64.0 (PyPI, 6 Oct 2026), MIT
note: Bayesian and frequentist experiment analysis with CUPED and running-time calculator; docs explain the statistics in plain language. Free tier: 1 million feature-flag requests and 1 million events per month.
course_use: Platform walkthrough; docs as reading on Bayesian vs. frequentist reporting. Free tier, then usage-based pricing.

title: Statsig
author_source: Statsig (acquired by OpenAI Sept 2025; product, brand and customers taken over by Amplitude May 2026); Python SDK statsig 0.72.1 (PyPI, 19 Aug 2026), ISC
note: Commercial experimentation and feature-flag platform with CUPED, sequential testing, SRM and holdouts; its Perspectives blog is a good practitioner reading source. Ownership changes are themselves a talking point on the experimentation tool market.
course_use: Industry context and guest-talk topic; free developer tier available (check current terms after Amplitude takeover).

title: Eppo (Datadog Experiments)
author_source: Eppo, acquired by Datadog May 2025, now branded Datadog Experiments; Python SDK eppo-server-sdk 4.4.1 (PyPI, 7 Jan 2026), MIT
note: Warehouse-native experimentation platform known for CUPED++, sequential and Bayesian analysis and strong statistical documentation; integrates experimentation with observability.
course_use: Industry context; documentation as reading. Commercial, pricing on request.

title: Optimizely Web Experimentation
author_source: Optimizely, commercial SaaS; Stats Engine based on always-valid inference (Johari et al.)
note: Market leader in website A/B testing for marketing teams; visual editor, Stats Engine with sequential testing and FDR control, i.e. a real-world implementation of mSPRT.
course_use: Case illustration of sequential testing in practice. Paid, enterprise pricing on request.

title: VWO (Visual Website Optimizer)
author_source: Wingify, commercial SaaS for testing and CRO
note: Widely used marketer-facing tool with visual editor, Bayesian SmartStats reporting, heatmaps; useful to show what non-technical marketing teams see.
course_use: Demo of a marketer-facing testing UI; free trial, paid plans.

title: AB Tasty
author_source: AB Tasty (France), commercial SaaS for experimentation and personalisation
note: European vendor popular in retail and e-commerce (Bayesian reporting, personalisation, feature experimentation); relevant for DACH employers.
course_use: Industry context, potential guest speaker company. Paid, pricing on request.

title: Unleash
author_source: Unleash (Bricks Software AS, Norway), open source feature-flag server Apache-2.0; Python SDK UnleashClient 6.8.0 (PyPI, 21 Jul 2026), MIT
note: Open source feature flags with gradual rollouts and variants; shows the randomisation and assignment layer (sticky hashing) separately from the analysis layer.
course_use: Short demo on how users are bucketed into variants. Open source, free self-hosted.

title: Mixpanel (Experiments report)
author_source: Mixpanel Inc., product analytics SaaS; Python SDK mixpanel 5.4.0 (PyPI, 2 Sep 2026), Apache-2.0
note: Event analytics with an experiments report that reads results of tests run in other flagging tools; illustrates the analytics-side workflow in digital marketing teams.
course_use: Industry context; free tier for students. Freemium.

title: pwr (R)
author_source: Stephane Champely et al., R package on CRAN, GPL-3
note: Cohen-style power functions (pwr.2p.test for two proportions, pwr.t.test); compact and well known from methods courses, useful for an R/Python comparison in Quarto.
course_use: Optional R exercise for power analysis. Open source, free. CRAN not reachable from this session, check version.

title: grf (R) - generalized random forests
author_source: Tibshirani, Athey, Wager et al., R package on CRAN, GPL-3
note: Reference implementation of causal forests with honest splitting, doubly robust ATE, best linear projection and RATE/Qini metrics for targeting; excellent vignettes.
course_use: Advanced lab on heterogeneous treatment effects, R alternative to EconML. Open source, free. Check current version.

title: Evan Miller A/B testing tools (sample size calculator, chi-squared test, sequential sampling)
author_source: Evan Miller, free web calculators
note: Classic browser calculators for sample size, two-proportion test, sequential sampling and t-tests; paired with his essay How Not To Run an A/B Test on peeking.
course_use: In-class warm-up before coding power analysis in Python. Free, no login.

title: Criteo Uplift Prediction Dataset (v2.1)
author_source: Criteo AI Lab (Diemert et al. 2018/2021), 13,979,592 rows, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial; check on download page)
note: Pooled incrementality tests from display advertising: 12 anonymised features f0-f11, treatment (85/15 split), exposure, visit (about 4.7 percent), conversion (about 0.29 percent). Ideal for ITT vs. treatment-on-treated, uplift models and power with rare outcomes. Also loadable via sklift.fetch_criteo.
course_use: Project data for uplift and incrementality; subsample for labs. Free download, academic use.

title: Criteo Attribution Modeling for Bidding Dataset
author_source: Criteo AI Lab, about 16.5 million impressions, 45k conversions, 700 campaigns, 30 days of traffic; non-commercial licence (check)
note: Impression-level log with click, conversion and whether the conversion was attributed to Criteo; used to contrast last-click attribution with causal (experimental) measurement. Not itself randomised.
course_use: Discussion and lab: why attribution is not incrementality. Free download; also on Hugging Face and Kaggle mirrors.

title: Hillstrom MineThatData E-Mail Analytics Challenge
author_source: Kevin Hillstrom, MineThatData (2008), 64,000 customers, about 5 MB CSV, free for research and teaching
note: Real retail email RCT: customers randomised to Mens email, Womens email or no email (about 21.3k each); covariates recency, history, mens, womens, zip_code, newbie, channel; outcomes visit, conversion, spend over two weeks. The best single dataset for a semester of A/B, CUPED-style adjustment and uplift exercises. Also in TensorFlow Datasets.
course_use: Main lab dataset (multi-arm test, revenue metric, HTE). Free, no login via sklift.fetch_hillstrom.

title: Marketing A/B Testing (ad vs. PSA)
author_source: Favio Vazquez, Kaggle dataset, 588,101 users, licence on Kaggle page
note: Users assigned to ad or public service announcement (PSA, ghost-ad style control, 96/4 split); variables test group, converted, total ads, most ads day, most ads hour. Lift about 2.55 vs 1.79 percent; strong dose-response by exposure, which invites a discussion of post-treatment conditioning.
course_use: Lab on two-proportion test with unbalanced allocation and PSA controls. Free with Kaggle login.

title: Cookie Cats mobile game A/B test
author_source: Kaggle dataset (yufengsui, from DataCamp project), 90,189 players, licence on Kaggle page
note: Gate at level 30 (control) vs. level 40; variables userid, version, sum_gamerounds, retention_1, retention_7. 7-day retention drops about 0.8 pp. Good for retention metrics, bootstrap CIs and heavy-tailed engagement data.
course_use: Warm-up lab on proportion tests and bootstrap. Free with Kaggle login.

title: E-commerce landing page A/B test (Udacity ab_data.csv)
author_source: Udacity Data Analyst Nanodegree project data, 294,478 rows, 5 columns; mirrored on Kaggle and GitHub
note: user_id, timestamp, group, landing_page, converted (about 12 percent conversion), plus countries.csv for segment analysis. Contains about 3,900 mismatched group/page rows and a duplicate user, a realistic data-cleaning and SRM teaching moment.
course_use: First lab: clean, check assignment integrity, z-test, logistic regression. Free.

title: Fast Food Marketing Campaign A/B Test
author_source: Kaggle dataset (chebotinaa, originally IBM Watson Analytics sample), 548 rows, 7 columns
note: Three promotions randomised across store locations, weekly sales over four weeks; MarketID, MarketSize, LocationID, AgeOfStore, Promotion, week, SalesInThousands. Small and retail-specific: ANOVA, cluster structure (stores in markets), repeated weeks.
course_use: Lab on multi-arm tests, post-hoc comparisons and clustering by market. Free with Kaggle login.

title: X5 RetailHero uplift dataset
author_source: X5 Retail Group (Russia) RetailHero competition 2019, via scikit-uplift fetch_x5; clients, train and purchases tables (purchase log several million rows)
note: Grocery retailer SMS campaign with treatment_flg and purchase target, client demographics and raw transaction history before the communication. Requires feature engineering from purchases, which makes it a realistic retail project.
course_use: Student project on uplift targeting with feature engineering. Free via sklift.

title: Lenta uplift dataset
author_source: Lenta (Russian hypermarket chain) via scikit-uplift fetch_lenta, about 687k customers and about 190 features
note: SMS campaign RCT for a grocery retailer: group (test/control), response_att (visit), gender, age, store type and many purchase-behaviour aggregates. Large but tidy; good for CATE and Qini curves.
course_use: Project data for uplift modelling. Free via sklift.

title: MegaFon Uplift Competition dataset (synthetic)
author_source: MegaFon (telecom) via scikit-uplift fetch_megafon, 600,000 rows, 50 features, synthetic
note: Synthetic data designed to resemble real telecom campaigns; binary treatment and conversion. Clean benchmark when real data are too messy.
course_use: Benchmark for comparing uplift models. Free via sklift.

title: Open Bandit Dataset (ZOZOTOWN)
author_source: ZOZO Research, Saito et al. (NeurIPS Datasets 2021), about 26 million impressions, CC BY 4.0 (check)
note: Logged data from an A/B test of two recommendation policies (Bernoulli Thompson sampling vs. uniform random) on a fashion e-commerce site with true propensity scores, item features and clicks; a 10k-row sample ships with obp.
course_use: Advanced lab on bandits and off-policy evaluation. Free download.

title: Upworthy Research Archive
author_source: Matias, Munger, Aubin Le Quere and Ebersole, Scientific Data 8 (2021); 32,487 headline experiments, 150,817 arms, 538 million assignments; open access on OSF
note: Headline and image package A/B tests (impressions and clicks per arm) from 2013-2015, split into exploratory and confirmatory sets. Lets students run thousands of tests, see the distribution of effects, winner's curse and multiple testing.
course_use: Lab on meta-analysis of many A/B tests, CTR copy testing; exploratory sample for projects. Free, open access.

title: Udacity Free Trial Screener experiment
author_source: Udacity and Google A/B Testing course (UD257) final project, two CSVs (control, experiment) with about 37 days of daily aggregates
note: Daily pageviews, clicks, enrollments, payments for control and treatment; teaches invariant vs. evaluation metrics, sanity checks, unit of diversion (cookie vs. user-id) and Bonferroni. Course itself is free on Udacity.
course_use: Lab on metric design and sanity checks with aggregated data. Free.

title: Starbucks rewards app offer data (Udacity capstone)
author_source: Starbucks and Udacity Data Scientist Nanodegree, simulated; portfolio (10 offers), profile (17,000 customers), transcript (306,534 events); JSON
note: Simulated BOGO, discount and informational offers with demographics and event logs. Not a clean RCT, so useful for discussing what is missing compared with a proper experiment and for offer-response modelling.
course_use: Project data with critical discussion of design. Free via GitHub mirrors; licence unclear, teaching use only.

title: Geo experiment sample data (GeoexperimentsResearch and GeoLift)
author_source: Google GeoexperimentsResearch (100 geos, daily sales and ad cost from 2015) and Meta GeoLift (GeoLift_PreTest / GeoLift_Test, US cities, daily conversions); both open source
note: Ready-made panel data for market selection, power simulation and synthetic-control or TBR analysis of geo lift tests.
course_use: Lab on geo experiments; data load with the packages. Free.

title: Replication data: The Surrogate Index (Athey, Chetty, Imbens, Kang)
author_source: Opportunity Insights, Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/QCKJYL
note: Code and (simulated/public) data to reproduce surrogate index estimates of long-term effects from short-term outcomes; transferable to CLV or retention as long-run marketing outcomes.
course_use: Advanced reading lab on long-term effects. Free, open access.

title: Yahoo! Front Page Today Module click log (R6)
author_source: Yahoo Webscope, R6A/R6B, about 45 million user visits with uniformly random article display; academic licence on application
note: The classic benchmark for unbiased offline evaluation of contextual bandits (Li et al. 2010/2011): random logging policy enables replay evaluation of news recommendation.
course_use: Background for bandit session; access requires university application. Free for research, login.

title: Synthetic experiment generators (causalml.dataset, dowhy.datasets, tea-tasting make_users_data)
author_source: Uber CausalML, PyWhy DoWhy and tea-tasting packages, open source
note: Functions such as synthetic_data(mode=1..4), make_uplift_classification, linear_dataset and make_users_data simulate experiments with known true effects, so students can check whether estimators recover the truth and run power simulations.
course_use: Simulation labs on power, CUPED gains and HTE recovery. Free, open source.

title: Two-sample proportion test, chi-square and Welch t-test
author_source: Kohavi, Tang and Xu (2020) Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments, Cambridge University Press, ch. 2 and 17; companion site experimentguide.com
note: Baseline inference for conversion (z-test, chi-square) and revenue per user (Welch t-test, CLT with large n, bootstrap for heavy tails). Chapter 1 is a free download on the companion site.
course_use: Session 1 reading and lab with statsmodels and scipy. Book paid (about 40 EUR), WU-Lizenz prüfen; chapter 1 free.

title: Power analysis, sample size and minimum detectable effect (MDE)
author_source: Key reference: All about sample-size calculations for A/B testing: novel extensions and practical guide (arXiv 2305.16459, 2023)
note: Covers sample size for proportions and means, ratio metrics, unequal allocation, multiple arms and how MDE trades off against test duration; connects to the 16 sigma squared over delta squared rule of thumb.
course_use: Lab: compute duration for a retail test given traffic; compare with Evan Miller calculator. Free, open access.

title: Sample ratio mismatch (SRM) check
author_source: Fabijan, Gupchup, Gupta, Omhover, Qin, Vermeer and Dmitriev (2019), KDD, Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments
note: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test on group counts as the first trust check; taxonomy of SRM causes (assignment, execution, log processing, interference, bots) with rules of thumb.
course_use: Reading plus 10-minute lab step on every dataset. Free PDF.

title: CUPED / CUPAC variance reduction (regression adjustment)
author_source: Deng, Xu, Kohavi and Walker (2013), WSDM, Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments by Utilizing Pre-Experiment Data, doi 10.1145/2433396.2433413
note: Uses pre-period covariates as control variates; about 50 percent variance reduction at Bing. CUPAC (DoorDash) replaces the covariate with an ML prediction. Equivalent to ANCOVA/OLS with centred covariate, a link business students know.
course_use: Lab with tea-tasting or OLS on Hillstrom (history as covariate). Paper free on exp-platform.com.

title: Sequential testing: mSPRT and always-valid p-values
author_source: Johari, Koomen, Pekelis and Walsh (2022), Operations Research 70(3), 1806-1821, Always Valid Inference: Continuous Monitoring of A/B Tests, doi 10.1287/opre.2021.2135
note: Explains why peeking inflates false positives and how mixture SPRT gives p-values valid at any stopping time; basis of Optimizely's Stats Engine. arXiv preprint 1512.04922 is free.
course_use: Simulation lab: peeking inflates type I error; then apply always-valid test. Preprint free.

title: Group sequential designs and alpha spending
author_source: Spotify Engineering (2023), Choosing a Sequential Testing Framework: Comparisons and Discussions; classic: O'Brien and Fleming (1979), Lan and DeMets (1983)
note: Practitioner comparison of group sequential tests vs. always-valid approaches with simulation evidence; implemented in spotify-confidence.
course_use: Reading for the sequential testing session. Free.

title: Bayesian A/B testing (Beta-Binomial, probability to beat control, expected loss)
author_source: PyMC example gallery: Introduction to Bayesian A/B Testing (PyMC Labs); critical view: Deng (2015) Objective Bayesian two sample hypothesis testing for online controlled experiments, WWW
note: Conjugate and PyMC models for conversion and revenue, decision rules based on expected loss; discuss priors and why Bayesian results are not immune to peeking problems.
course_use: Lab in PyMC or Bambi; compare to frequentist result on the same data. Free.

title: Multiple testing corrections (Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg)
author_source: Benjamini and Hochberg (1995), Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B 57(1), 289-300, doi 10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x
note: Needed for many metrics, segments and arms; FDR vs. FWER, primary vs. guardrail metrics; Upworthy archive shows the problem at scale.
course_use: Lab with statsmodels multipletests on segment analyses. Paper paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Ratio metrics and the delta method
author_source: Deng, Knoblich and Lu (2018), KDD, Applying the Delta Method in Metric Analytics: A Practical Guide with Novel Ideas, arXiv 1803.06336
note: Click-through rate, revenue per session or basket size have randomisation unit (user) different from analysis unit; naive t-tests understate variance. Delta method gives correct standard errors.
course_use: Lab with tea-tasting ratio metrics. Free preprint.

title: Geo experiments and synthetic control (incl. cluster randomisation)
author_source: Vaver and Koehler (2011), Measuring Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments, Google; Abadie (2021), Journal of Economic Literature 59(2), Using Synthetic Controls; implemented in GeoLift
note: When users cannot be randomised (TV, offline stores, privacy limits), randomise or match markets and build counterfactuals; covers power with few clusters and iROAS.
course_use: Session on offline/omnichannel retail; GeoLift docs as hands-on guide. Free.

title: Switchback experiments
author_source: Bojinov, Simchi-Levi and Zhao (2023), Management Science 69(7), 3759-3777, Design and Analysis of Switchback Experiments, doi 10.1287/mnsc.2022.4583
note: Alternate treatment over time periods when units interfere (pricing, delivery fees, marketplace algorithms); optimal period length under carryover effects; randomisation inference.
course_use: Reading for advanced session on marketplace and pricing experiments. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen; HBS working paper free.

title: Difference-in-differences and Bayesian structural time series (CausalImpact) as quasi-experiments
author_source: Brodersen, Gallusser, Koehler, Remy and Scott (2015), Annals of Applied Statistics 9(1), Inferring causal impact using Bayesian structural time-series models, doi 10.1214/14-AOAS788; Cunningham, Causal Inference: The Mixtape, ch. 9
note: For campaigns launched without randomisation: parallel trends, event-study plots, and BSTS counterfactuals; contrast with RCT evidence (Gordon et al. 2019).
course_use: Lab with tfcausalimpact or statsmodels DiD regression. Paper open access; Mixtape free online.

title: Multi-armed bandits and Thompson sampling
author_source: Russo, Van Roy, Kazerouni, Osband and Wen (2018), A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling, Foundations and Trends in ML, arXiv 1707.02038; marketing application: Schwartz, Bradlow and Fader (2017), Marketing Science 36(4), doi 10.1287/mksc.2016.1023
note: Adaptive allocation to minimise regret during the test (display ads, headlines, offers); trade-off between earning and learning, and the bias of estimates from adaptive designs.
course_use: Simulation lab with MABWiser; Schwartz et al. as marketing reading (WU-Lizenz prüfen). Tutorial free.

title: Heterogeneous treatment effects and uplift: meta-learners (S, T, X, R, DR)
author_source: Kuenzel, Sekhon, Bickel and Yu (2019), PNAS 116(10), 4156-4165, Metalearners for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects using machine learning, doi 10.1073/pnas.1804597116
note: Framework behind CausalML and EconML; Qini/uplift curves for targeting decisions; links A/B testing to customer targeting and CRM.
course_use: Lab on Hillstrom or Criteo with CausalML. Open access.

title: Causal forests and targeting on treatment effect (not risk)
author_source: Wager and Athey (2018), JASA 113(523), doi 10.1080/01621459.2017.1319839; marketing application: Ascarza (2018), Journal of Marketing Research 55(1), 80-98, Retention Futility, doi 10.1509/jmr.16.0163
note: Ascarza shows with two field experiments that targeting customers with highest churn risk is less effective than targeting by estimated sensitivity to the intervention; causal forests (grf, EconML) estimate that sensitivity.
course_use: Core reading for the uplift session; lab with grf or EconML. JMR paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Interference and experiments in two-sided marketplaces
author_source: Johari, Li, Liskovich and Weintraub (2022), Management Science 68(10), Experimental Design in Two-Sided Platforms: An Analysis of Bias, doi 10.1287/mnsc.2021.4247
note: SUTVA violations when treated and control buyers compete for the same supply (Airbnb, eBay, ride-hailing); customer-side vs. listing-side randomisation and bias direction.
course_use: Reading for advanced session on platforms. Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen; arXiv preprint free.

title: Long-term effects and surrogate indices
author_source: Athey, Chetty, Imbens and Kang, The Surrogate Index, NBER Working Paper 26463 (2019), Review of Economic Studies (2026)
note: Combines short-term outcomes into an index predicting long-term outcomes (e.g. CLV, retention) under surrogacy assumptions; motivates holdout groups and novelty/primacy discussion.
course_use: Reading for the session on short-term metrics vs. long-term value. Free working paper.

title: Ghost ads, PSA controls and advertising lift tests
author_source: Johnson, Lewis and Nubbemeyer (2017), Journal of Marketing Research 54(6), 867-884, Ghost Ads: Improving the Economics of Measuring Online Ad Effectiveness, doi 10.1509/jmr.15.0297
note: Compares ITT, PSA and ghost-ad designs for ad experiments; ghost ads log the would-be exposures in control, raising precision by an order of magnitude at lower cost. Retargeting case: plus 17 percent visits, 10.5 percent purchases.
course_use: Core reading for ad incrementality; pairs with the Kaggle ad vs. PSA data. SSRN version free.

title: Intent-to-treat vs. treatment-on-the-treated (non-compliance, exposure)
author_source: Gordon, Zettelmeyer, Bhargava and Chapsky (2019), Marketing Science 38(2), 193-225, A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook, doi 10.1287/mksc.2018.1135
note: 15 Facebook lift experiments with 500 million user observations: ITT, exposure-based effects via Wald/IV scaling, and why observational methods overestimate ad effects. Also Blake, Nosko and Tadelis (2015) Econometrica on eBay paid search.
course_use: Reading and lab with Criteo uplift (treatment vs. exposure columns). Paywalled, WU-Lizenz prüfen; MSI working paper version free.

title: Off-policy evaluation of recommendation and targeting policies
author_source: Saito, Aihara, Matsutani and Narita (2021), Open Bandit Dataset and Pipeline: Towards Realistic and Reproducible Off-Policy Evaluation, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks, arXiv 2008.07146
note: Evaluate a new policy with logged randomised data (IPW, doubly robust) before an online test; shows how experiments generate reusable data assets.
course_use: Advanced reading with obp lab. Free preprint.

title: Christina Schamp
author_source: WU Wien, Full Professor, Head of Institute for Digital Marketing and Behavioral Insights; Wien; academic
note: Behavioral experiments are the core of her work; runs lab and field experiments, e.g. pre-commitment pricing field experiment with a language-learning app, and the first field study of sales effects of cause-related marketing promotions in retail (Schamp, Heitmann, Peers, Leeflang, JMR 2024). Strongest WU match for experiments in digital marketing and retail.
course_use: Very good fit for an on-site guest lecture or Q&A in Vienna: how to set up a field experiment with a company partner, and what a JMR-level field study in retail looks like. English or German. Colleague in-house, easy to arrange.

title: Nils Wlömert
author_source: WU Wien, Professor of Marketing, Head of Institute for Retailing and Data Science (Stand Suchergebnis 2026); Wien; academic
note: Empirical work on digital platforms, streaming and media markets with causal inference methods (e.g. cancel-culture streaming study with Winkler and Liaukonyte). Responsible for the open WU course book Marketing Research Design and Analysis (imsmwu.github.io), with R code for hypothesis tests and experimental data analysis. Caution: a search snippet linked him to the auto-renewal newspaper field experiment, but that paper is by Miller, Sahni and Strulov-Shlain.
course_use: On-site input on analysing experimental and quasi-experimental marketing data in R; the MRDA materials can be reused in labs. German or English.

title: Martin Schreier
author_source: WU Wien, Professor of Marketing, Head of Department of Marketing and Institute for Marketing Management; Wien; academic
note: Co-author of two randomized field experiments in retail on the market value of crowdsourced products (Nishikawa, Schreier, Fuchs, Ogawa, JMR 2017, with Japanese retailer Muji). A retail field-experiment example rather than online A/B testing.
course_use: Short on-site talk or Q&A on running randomized field experiments in a retail context. German or English.

title: Daniel Winkler
author_source: Postdoctoral fellow UNSW Sydney School of Marketing and research fellow WU Wien (according to CV, Stand Suchergebnis; check current role); Wien / Global; academic
note: WU PhD; works on causal inference, Bayesian statistics and digital markets (streaming, social media boycotts). No experimentation-specific publication confirmed; the link to the topic is through causal-inference methods.
course_use: Remote session on causal inference for marketing data in R or Python. German or English. Location may be Sydney, which makes timing hard.

title: Julia Neidhardt
author_source: TU Wien Informatics, Assistant Professor, Head of Christian Doppler Lab for Recommender Systems in Multi-Domain Settings; Wien; academic
note: Her CD lab works with the Austrian media house Falter and YKMB on recommender systems. The industry partnership allows live observation of system changes over long periods, i.e. online evaluation and A/B testing of recommenders in news and tourism. Diversity and fairness of recommendations.
course_use: On-site guest talk on online experiments for recommender systems in Austrian media; good for the bridge between offline metrics and A/B tests. German or English.

title: Siegfried Stepke
author_source: e-dialog (Vienna analytics and Google Marketing Platform agency), founder and managing director; Wien; practitioner
note: Founder of the ProgrammatiCon conference in Vienna; presented Google Optimize 360 testing and personalisation and the Google Marketing Platform including testing. Long-standing speaker at Austrian analytics conferences. Optimize has since been discontinued, so ask about current testing tools.
course_use: Practitioner guest talk in Vienna on how Austrian brands organise testing, analytics and personalisation in agencies. German, likely English too.

title: Thomas Tauchner
author_source: JENTIS (Vienna, server-side tracking), CEO and co-founder; earlier founder of analytics agency Webrocket; Wien; practitioner
note: Indirect topic link: consent loss and tracking gaps distort conversion data and therefore experiment results. JENTIS Synthetic Users (2024) model untracked conversions for ad networks. Speaker at SUPERWEEK 2023 and 2025.
course_use: Guest talk in Vienna on data quality, GDPR consent and measurement limits for A/B tests and campaign experiments. German or English. Note: this is a vendor perspective.

title: Armin Larndorfer
author_source: KlickImpuls (Linz agency), contact for tracking and CRO, over 15 years experience; Österreich; practitioner
note: Weakly evidenced: named on agency page as CRO and tracking lead. No public talks or publications on experimentation found.
course_use: Possible remote or on-site practitioner talk on CRO for Austrian SMEs. German. Check speaking experience first.

title: Matthias Wieser
author_source: Lecturer, Master Digital Marketing and Kommunikation, FH St. Pölten (USTP); Österreich; practitioner / lecturer
note: Weakly evidenced: FH news names him for student projects on website analysis and conversion optimization with Google Analytics, Hotjar and UsabilityHub. No dedicated experimentation publications found.
course_use: Peer exchange about teaching CRO projects; possible short practitioner input. German.

title: Ron Kohavi
author_source: Independent consultant and Maven instructor; formerly Airbnb, Microsoft (ExP), Amazon; Global; practitioner / communicator
note: Lead author of Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (Cambridge UP 2020, with Tang and Xu), the reference book for A/B testing. Teaches Maven courses Accelerating Innovation with A/B Testing and Advanced Topics in Practical A/B Testing (cohorts Oct and Nov/Dec 2026). Twyman's law, OEC, sample ratio mismatch.
course_use: Top choice for a remote keynote or recorded interview (English); his course and LinkedIn posts are good student resources. Likely paid consulting rates.

title: Diane Tang
author_source: Google, Google Fellow (Stand Wissensstand; check current role); Global; practitioner
note: Co-author of Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments; lead author of 'Overlapping Experiment Infrastructure: More, Better, Faster Experimentation' (KDD 2010), which describes Google's layered experiment system.
course_use: Recorded interview or remote Q&A on experiment infrastructure at scale. English. Hard to book.

title: Ya Xu
author_source: Formerly VP Engineering and Head of Data, LinkedIn (check current role); Global; practitioner
note: Co-author of Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments; built LinkedIn's XLNT experimentation platform; papers on network effects and A/B testing in social networks (KDD 2015).
course_use: Remote talk on experimentation culture and network interference. English. Current role not verified.

title: Lukas Vermeer
author_source: Vista, Senior Director of Experimentation (Stand Suchergebnis); formerly 8 years responsible for A/B testing at Booking.com; advisor to ABsmartly; Global; practitioner / communicator
note: Leading European voice on scaling experimentation (Booking.com culture, empowered teams, SRM checks). Has a speaker media kit and speaks frequently at conferences and on podcasts.
course_use: Very good remote guest lecture (Netherlands, English); open to speaking requests via media kit. A Booking.com case plus a live talk work well together.

title: Stefan Thomke
author_source: Harvard Business School, Professor of Business Administration (check current title); German-born; Global (DACH roots); academic
note: Author of Experimentation Works: The Surprising Power of Business Experiments (HBR Press 2020) and, with Kohavi, 'The Surprising Power of Online Experiments' (HBR 2017). HBS cases on Booking.com experimentation.
course_use: Book chapters and HBS cases for the managerial side; a remote talk is unlikely but a recorded HBR interview works. English, possibly German. Profile URL constructed.

title: Georgi Georgiev
author_source: Analytics-Toolkit.com, founder; Bulgaria; Global; practitioner / communicator
note: Author of Statistical Methods in Online A/B Testing (2019); writes on sequential testing (AGILE), power, minimum detectable effect and common statistical errors in CRO. Calculators can be used in class.
course_use: Remote guest session on test statistics and planning (English, European time zone). His blog and tools are good for labs.

title: Sean J. Taylor
author_source: Formerly Facebook Core Data Science and Lyft (head of rideshare labs); co-founder Motif Analytics (Stand Wissensstand; check current role); Global; practitioner / communicator
note: Prophet co-author; talks and threads on experimentation at Facebook and Lyft, marketplace experiments and switchback designs; field experiments on social influence (with Aral, Muchnik).
course_use: Remote talk or podcast clip on experimentation in two-sided marketplaces. English.

title: Dean Eckles
author_source: MIT Sloan School of Management, Associate Professor of Marketing (check current title); Global; academic
note: Formerly at Facebook; large-scale field experiments on peer effects and advertising, design of experiments under network interference, bootstrap for dependent data in online experiments.
course_use: Remote research talk for advanced students on interference and social advertising experiments. English.

title: Duncan J. Watts
author_source: University of Pennsylvania (Annenberg, Wharton, Engineering), Stevens University Professor; Global; academic
note: MusicLab experiment on social influence and success (Salganik, Dodds, Watts, Science 2006), a classic online experiment on social proof; also work on ad effectiveness at Yahoo and Microsoft Research.
course_use: Use MusicLab as a teaching example; a remote talk is unlikely. English.

title: Eytan Bakshy
author_source: Meta, leads Adaptive Experimentation group (Stand Wissensstand; check current role); Global; practitioner / academic
note: Creator of PlanOut (KDD 2014) and the open-source Ax / BoTorch platform for adaptive experiments and Bayesian optimisation; social advertising field experiments on Facebook (Bakshy et al. 2012).
course_use: Remote technical talk on adaptive experimentation and bandits; Ax tutorials for advanced labs. English.

title: Susan Athey
author_source: Stanford Graduate School of Business, Economics of Technology Professor; Global; academic
note: Causal machine learning (causal forests, heterogeneous treatment effects), contextual bandits and adaptive experiments; former chief economist at Microsoft and Bing experimentation background.
course_use: Recorded lectures (e.g. her ML and causal inference videos) instead of a live talk. English.

title: Garrett A. Johnson
author_source: Boston University Questrom School of Business, Associate Professor of Marketing (check title); Global; academic
note: Developed ghost ads for measuring ad effectiveness in field experiments (Johnson, Lewis, Nubbemeyer, JMR 2017); work on GDPR effects and on large-scale ad experiment meta-analyses.
course_use: Remote talk on ad-lift experiments and ghost ads; the ghost-ads paper is a core reading. English.

title: Brett R. Gordon
author_source: Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University, Professor of Marketing; Global; academic
note: Lead author of 'A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook' (Marketing Science 2019) and follow-up on whether observational methods can replace RCTs (2023).
course_use: Reading plus remote Q&A on why observational ad measurement fails. English.

title: Florian Zettelmeyer
author_source: Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University, Professor of Marketing; German; Global (DACH roots); academic
note: Co-author of the Facebook ad field experiments comparison (Marketing Science 2019); teaches analytics for managers with a focus on causal inference and experiments.
course_use: Remote talk for managers on experiments vs. observational data; German possible. English.

title: Elea McDonnell Feit
author_source: Drexel University LeBow College of Business, Associate Professor of Marketing; Global; academic
note: Test and Roll: profit-maximizing A/B tests (Feit and Berman, Marketing Science 2019); co-author of R for Marketing Research and Analytics; open A/B-testing workshop materials in R for marketers.
course_use: Very good teaching fit: her open workshop slides and R code can be used directly; remote guest session realistic. English.

title: Ron Berman
author_source: The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania, Assistant/Associate Professor of Marketing (check title); Global; academic
note: Test and Roll (with Feit); 'p-Hacking and False Discovery in A/B Testing' (with Pekelis, Scott, Van den Bulte) using Optimizely data; work on attribution.
course_use: Reading on p-hacking in A/B tests; remote Q&A. English.

title: Anja Lambrecht
author_source: London Business School, Professor of Marketing; German; Global (DACH roots); academic
note: Field experiments in online advertising: retargeting (Lambrecht and Tucker, JMR 2013), algorithmic bias in STEM job ads (Management Science 2019); measurement of digital marketing.
course_use: Remote guest lecture from London; German or English. Retargeting paper suits a class discussion.

title: Catherine Tucker
author_source: MIT Sloan School of Management, Sloan Distinguished Professor of Management and Professor of Marketing; Global; academic
note: Many field experiments in digital advertising and privacy (e.g. Goldfarb and Tucker on privacy regulation and ad effectiveness, retargeting with Lambrecht); co-chairs research on digital economy.
course_use: Recorded talks and papers; a remote talk is possible but hard to book. English.

title: Navdeep S. Sahni
author_source: Stanford Graduate School of Business, Associate Professor of Marketing (check title); Global; academic
note: Field experiments on search advertising, ad signalling and subscriptions; co-author of 'Sophisticated Consumers with Inertia' (Miller, Sahni, Strulov-Shlain): auto-renewal contracts tested on over 1 million readers of a European newspaper lowered take-up by 35 percent.
course_use: Subscription field experiment as a retail and pricing case; remote Q&A. English.

title: Klaus M. Miller
author_source: HEC Paris, Assistant Professor of Marketing (check title); German; Global (DACH); academic
note: Lead author of the large newspaper subscription field experiment on auto-renewal (SSRN 4065098, AEA RCT registry); research on digital news pricing and privacy in online advertising.
course_use: Remote guest talk in German or English on running a million-user pricing experiment with a publisher; geographically close (Paris).

title: Steven Tadelis
author_source: UC Berkeley Haas School of Business, Professor of Economics, Business and Public Policy; Global; academic
note: eBay paid-search experiment showing brand-keyword ads had near-zero returns (Blake, Nosko, Tadelis, Econometrica 2015), a key case for why experiments beat attribution; former eBay and Amazon economist.
course_use: The eBay study as a lecture case; remote Q&A. English.

title: Ramesh Johari
author_source: Stanford University, Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Global; academic
note: Always-valid p-values and sequential testing behind Optimizely's Stats Engine (Johari, Pekelis, Walsh, Koomen); marketplace experiment design and interference.
course_use: Reading on peeking problems; remote technical talk. English.

title: Aleksander Fabijan
author_source: Microsoft, Experimentation Platform (ExP), data scientist / product manager (Stand Wissensstand; check current role); Slovenian; Global; practitioner / academic
note: PhD on experimentation growth; 'Experimentation growth: Evolving trustworthy A/B testing capabilities in online software companies' (Journal of Software: Evolution and Process 2018) and the Experimentation Evolution Model; many ExP papers on pitfalls.
course_use: Remote talk on experimentation maturity models; European time zone. English.

title: Maximilian Kasy
author_source: University of Oxford, Professor of Economics; Global; academic
note: Adaptive experimental design: exploration sampling for policy choice (Kasy and Sautmann, Econometrica 2021), adaptive targeted field experiment for refugees in Jordan; bridges bandits and classic RCTs.
course_use: Remote advanced talk on adaptive experiments and bandits. English.

title: Chetan Sharma
author_source: Eppo, founder and CEO (Eppo acquired by Datadog in 2025, Stand Wissensstand; check current role); formerly Airbnb and Webflow data; Global; practitioner
note: Built Eppo, a warehouse-native experimentation platform with CUPED and sequential tests; frequent writer and podcast guest on experimentation culture.
